name: AbilityAboveStockBoundaryHasNoMpCheckOrCost
summary: The MP check and payment (sub_1402828E4) and its preview twin (sub_14030B1A0) only look at ids up to 0x16F (367): an ability id above that boundary pays no MP, has no MP check and shows no cost.

behavior.text: sub_1402828E4 reads the unit's command byte (+0x1A1) and ability word (+0x1A2), looks the kind up in g_CommandKind and clears g_AbilityMpCost; a unit with status mask 0x04 at +0x65 or a non-zero sub_14030DD1C answer returns that answer + 6; a Toad unit (+0x63 mask 0x02) returns 5 unless the ability is 0, 367 or 29 (a kind of 10 returns 5 whatever the ability).
an id above 0x16F skips the rest and returns 0; otherwise, for a kind-0 or kind-6 command, the action row's flag byte +5 mask 0x20 together with the unit's +0x62 mask 0x08 returns 2.

for kind 0, a job byte other than 93 and an id up to 0x16F: the cost is action-row byte +13, halved when unit +0x99 has bit 7; it is stored in g_AbilityMpCost; if the unit's MP (+0x34) is below it the function returns 3; otherwise MP is paid unless the simulate mode is 2.
sub_14030B1A0 is the same chain without the payment or the return 3: it only stores the cost.
the equality tests against 367 at 0x14020CB7F (sub_14020CB0C), 0x14026B693 (sub_14026B310), 0x140282960 and 0x14030B202 are the four single-id tests of this boundary.

notes: The return codes 2, 3 and 5 are read as values; their consumers were not traced.
open_questions: ? the consumers of the return codes.

name: AbilityListWordsCarryFlags
summary: An ability list word holds the ability id in bits 0..9 and flags above it (0x800 equipped or innate, 0x1000 learned, 0x4000 greyed); every consumer strips them with & 0x3FF before the id is stored or looked up. Widening such a mask for item ids leaks the flags into the stored ability word.

behavior.text: sub_140333338 tests 0x4000, 0x1000 and 0x800 on the word, then stores word & 0x3FF through sub_14028916C; sub_1403333F0 ORs 0x1000 into a combat-set word before calling it.
with the mask widened to 0xFFFF, the reaction ability 514 was stored as 0x1202 in the party and save records; the mask and sub_140366FE0's two (help key 0x7800 + id, history entry) are 0x3FF.
ability ids above 1023 need the flags moved out of the word first.

name: AbilityTextKeysPast2047
summary: The game names an ability by the 16-bit key pool << 11 | id (11 bits).

behavior.text: the ability text keys are 0x7000 + id (name, pool 14) and 0x7800 + id (help, pool 15); sub_140226208 takes 11 bits of the id, so 2047 is the last id with its own key.

44 producers build 0x7000 / 0x7800 + id; 32-bit carriers (S3, S5, the event queue) pass a 32-bit key, 16-bit ones (the S6 command cells, the timeline string arrays, the crystal list) truncate it; readers test (key & 0xF800) == 0x7000 and take id = key & 0x7FF; the info-window dword reads a negative value as none.
the help arrays read the word 0x7FF as none, so ability id 2047 is reserved; ability ids are loaded sign-extended in many places, so the ceiling is 0x7FFF.

the banner message row is pool * 1000 + (key & 0x7FF) (BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor, BattleMsg_ResolveEntry), so the game's text names an ability by key only below 1000: a derived row for ability 2015 replaced the 'Wait' banner (row 16015).

open_questions: ? the set-C crystal window (sub_140364408); the writers of the static help arrays (word_14186AF14 / 1E / 22).

name: AFailedMeshLoadSkipsEveryLaterRendererStep
summary: When MapMesh_Load returns anything but 0 (missing file, oversize, wrong header, ids 15 and 33) the texture, system-texture and anim steps are not run and the mesh set's loaded-id field stays at none; the map block's tile and polygon records are still applied.

behavior.text: the caller tests the result right after the call; only 0 leads to the texture reset, the id fields, the two texture loaders and the anim load.
with the loaded-id field at none, the polygon rebuild and the node timers do nothing.
the stock pack has RefinedBgTexture rows for maps 42, 97..99, 101 and 102 with no mesh file and no texture folder, which fits a silent skip.
what draws the sky gradient and the black deployment view when no mesh is loaded.

name: AFaultInAGameTaskFreezesTheGame
summary: Game logic runs in task threads that the main thread hands control to each frame (GameTasks_RunFrameSteps waits on them). A fault inside a task kills that thread without a crash: the main thread waits forever, the pad is no longer polled, and no dump is written.

behavior.text: an access violation in a scene task (sub_14030DD8C) froze the game on the deployment screen; the main thread sat in WaitForSingleObject inside GameTasks_RunFrameSteps, every task thread was parked in its wait, the pad poll count stopped, and Windows wrote no crash dump.

open_questions: ? where the task's fault is swallowed (a handler of the task runner).

name: AfterDamageReactionChain
summary: At the end of Battle_ApplyActionResult the unit held in g_BattleActingUnit is tested for passive reactions in a fixed order; the first one present goes to a Brave-roll helper, and the reaction executor then handles only the ids it has a case for.

behavior.text: the chain runs unless the formula result's type byte (0x1407B0788) is 7 or sub_14030AF88 answers non-zero; then it tests, in order: +0x94 bit 0x80 (id 422), 0x40 (423), 0x20 (424), 0x02 (428), +0x95 bit 0x40 (431), 0x20 (432), 0x10 (433), 0x08 (434, through sub_14030BE68), +0x96 bit 0x40 (439), 0x10 (441); only the first bit found acts.

sub_14030BE18 requires the action block's flag byte +39 bit 7, passes without a roll in a simulation or rolls Rng_Percent on the unit's Brave byte (+0x2B), and stores the reaction id at block word +16 and copies the HP result (block word +6) to word +40.
sub_14030BE68 additionally requires the unit's status byte +0x63 bit 0x01 and only stores the reaction id at word +16.

sub_1403095E4 (run first by Battle_ResolveAction when the battle-state gate is non-zero) refuses ids whose g_ReactionGateTable byte has 1 in its low two bits (returns 0) and handles the cases 422..434, 438, 439, 444 and 446; any other id clears block byte +39 and returns -1.
the compare chain has no case for 435..437 and 440..443 and has cases 444 and 446; the ids 442 and 443 are dropped.

notes: In Battle_ResolveAction g_BattleActingUnit is set from the second argument (the target slot of the action being resolved); which record it holds inside Battle_ApplyActionResult was not traced, the chain reads whatever record it holds.
open_questions: ? what the cases 444 and 446 are; which reaction names the ids carry (not read here).

name: AiJudgesStatusesThroughTheFortyBitSetsAndAValueTable
summary: An AI-controlled unit weighs statuses in two places, both limited to the 40 statuses of the five status bytes: the test of whether an action is worth trying on a unit compares the action's status bytes (from its inflict row) with the unit's, and the score of a simulated outcome adds one fixed value per status the unit has (tbl_AiStatusValue).

behavior.text: Action_BuildCurrentAction copies the 5 status bytes of the action's inflict row into g_AiCurrentAction +8..+12 and the ability's AI hint bytes (aux row +4..+7) into +13..+16.

Ai_ActionWorthOnUnit finds an action worth trying when it would add a status the unit lacks and is not immune to, or remove one the unit has, is not innate and will not wear off before the action resolves.

Battle_AITurnRun scores the simulated outcome per unit as HP x 128 / max HP, plus tbl_AiStatusValue[s] for each status s (0..39) the unit has (Blindness and Silence scaled by a unit value / 4; Charmed, Vampire, Confusion halved under some conditions), plus an MP term; units of the acting side count positive, the others negative.
the scale: full HP is worth 128, KO -192, Poison -26, Haste +19.
the AI's trials run with g_BattleSimulating (0x14186AF80) set; Ai_UnitTurnStep sets it before the first stage and clears it when the planner is done.
whether the simulation runs later turns (turn-end damage, status countdowns) before the score is taken.

name: AnUnservedIdFromASaveFreezesTheGame
scope: loading a save whose item ids have no row
summary: The game trusts every id in a save: an equipped item with no item row reaches the unit stat builder, which reads the armor record it does not get and faults inside a game task, freezing the game.

behavior.text: seen live 2026-11-11: slot 50 held items 300 and 3000 (no item row) in two units' hands (save record +0x14); walking into the Dorter story battle faulted at 0x140277B94 in Unit_ApplyEquipment (a byte read through the null result of Item_GetArmorRecord for that id) in a game task; the game froze (no dump; `dbg.py exceptions` showed the fault).

open_questions: ? other unchecked ids of a save the game trusts the same way (a job or skillset word with no row).

name: AttackWeaponReach
scope: battle: the tiles the Attack command can target, from the equipped weapon or bare hands
summary: Which tiles a unit's basic Attack can target: one weapon is chosen, its flag byte picks one of four shapes (strike, lunge, direct, arc), heights are compared in half-steps, the unit's own tile and some flagged tiles are removed.

behavior.text: weapon = the item at unit +0x20; if empty (0xFF) or not below 0x105, the item at +0x24; if that too, item 0 = bare hands (range 1, flags 0x88). Toad (+0x63 bit 0x02) always uses item 0. With two weapons only the +0x20 one decides the reach.

flags bit 0x80 (strike: bare hands, knives, swords, katanas, axes, rods, staves, flails, bags): the four adjacent tiles whose target height is within [H - 6, H + 5] half-steps of the attacker's reach height H.

flags bit 0x40 without 0x80 (lunge: spears, poles, cloths): the four adjacent tiles within [H - 8, H + 7] and the four tiles two away in straight lines within [H - 6, H + 7]; no diagonal, the tile between is not tested.
flags bit 0x20 without 0xC0 (direct: guns 8, crossbows 4, harps 3, books 3): every tile at Manhattan distance 3 up to the range, any height.
none of 0xE0 (arc: bows, flags 0x15, range 5): every tile at distance d >= 3 with d - trunc((H - t) / 4) <= range, t the target's half-step height.

target height t = (b3 & 0x1F) + 2 * (b2 + (b3 >> 5)) of the target tile in its own layer; H = (b3 & 0x1F) + 2 * b2 of the attacker's tile, +2 when mounted, +2 when floating (+0x9E bit 3 or status Float), plus the depth term only for floating or +0x9E bits 7 / 6 (Unit_GetReachHeight).

both layers of a tile are judged separately; the attacker's own tile is removed (BattleRange_MarkAttack); tiles with byte +6 bit 0x02 lose their mark, and tiles with byte +6 bit 0x01 or surface 0x3F are not flagged targetable.
the weapon's range byte is used only by the direct and arc shapes; strike reach is always 1 and lunge reach always 2.
'H - 6 .. H + 5' in whole steps = a target 3 steps lower up to 2.5 steps higher for a strike; matches the live note that from height 0 a target 3 higher was not yellow.
the shapes do not look at units: a tile is a target whether empty or occupied (live: yellow tiles include empty ones).

notes: The debugger models these rules (its reach module, with an offline self-test). Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? Not yet seen live: the minimum distance 3 of direct weapons (guns, crossbows, harps, books), the bow height bonus, the lunge bands. ? What decides white versus red-with-slash outside the yellow set (not in these builders).

name: BattleAbilityListReadsLearnedBitsThroughAPointerPastTheGroup
summary: The battle's usable-ability list builder reads the three learned bytes of a job group from a battle record with the group number in one address register and the record pointer plus twice the group in the other, so for a large group neither register points into the record that is read.

behavior.text: at 0x14030E55A the group is widened, then three one-byte loads at 0x14030E561, 0x14030E56D and 0x14030E57A read the record's learned array at +0xA2, +0xA3 and +0xA4 for that group (3 bytes a group) and join them into one 24-bit mask, high byte first.
the address is the group plus a register holding the record address plus twice the group; the record address itself stays in the register that holds the unit's record through the function.
with a group of 24 or more the pointer register lies past the 512-byte record's stock array, and from a group of about 104 past the record, inside the next battle record of the unit table.

with the group of a unit's own job read from outside the stock array, the job's command opened its list only when these three reads returned that job's learned bits; reading other bytes gave the red 'Unable to use' banner.

notes: The same split of offset and pointer as JobArrayAccessesPutTheRecordPointerInTheIndexRegister, with the pointer register advanced by twice the group.

name: BattleActionJpFormulaAndSpillover
summary: JP for an action is 8 + 2 x the job level of the acting unit's current job + the unit's level / 4, scaled by an event percentage and by JP Boost; every other unit of the battle gets a quarter of that base amount in the same job slot.

behavior.text: the base amount is zero when the action earned no experience; otherwise (unit level >> 2) + 8 + 2 x the job level nibble of the slot Job_IdToIndex gives for the unit's job byte; units with flag 0x20 in byte +6 get nothing.
each of the 21 battle units except the actor receives base >> 2 through Unit_AwardJobJp in that same job slot (the award itself refuses units of another team).

the actor receives base x percent / 100 (the percent is 100 unless a shop-mode table row sets another), then x 1.5 with integer arithmetic when byte +153 has bit 0x40 (JP Boost), or x 1.5 in floating point when the unit's word at +504 has bit 0x800; Unit_AwardJobJp caps at 9999.

name: BattleCommandHeaderTakesTheUnitsJobByte
summary: The header of the battle Abilities list (the job name and icon above the commands) is a job record built by sub_140335140: for the unit's own job command it takes the battle unit's job byte (+3); for a secondary command the job that owns the command's skillset.

behavior.text: with the command index 1 the job is the unit record's +3; otherwise UnitWork_FindJobBySkillset(unit, command); JobRecord_FromJobId then builds the header record.
the header names the job of the selected command.

name: BattleCommandMenuCarriesSetsAsBytes
summary: The battle command menu works with skillset ids as single bytes at every step: the unit's two set bytes, the byte lists the menu builders write, the kind array, the AI's command table and the command byte of the 20-byte action block. 0xFF ends every list, 0x18 is never listed, and set bytes are copied by Mem_CopyChecked.

behavior.text: sub_14030E010 builds the list for a unit: byte 0 = 1, then +0x12 (skipped when 0 or 0x18), +0x13 (skipped when 0), 2 and 3 from the passive bits at +0x9B (not for a Toad), then 0xFF; a unit with +0x65 bit 0x04 (or +0x1B4 bit 0x40 with dword_14185670C zero) gets 0xFF alone; a monster set (0xB0..0xDF in either byte) gives the primary set alone. It then fills g_BattleCommandKinds with g_CommandKind[byte] & 0xF for up to 6 entries.
sub_140217630 builds the same list (1, +0x12, +0x13, 0xFF; no 2 and 3) on a scratch unit in a stack array and asks sub_14030DD8C for each command with kind 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 or 10.
sub_140316B04 / sub_140316D24 write the AI's table: the command byte (the unit's set) goes to byte +2 of each entry, 0xFF ends the row.

the 20-byte action block at unit +0x1A0 (+1 command byte, +2 ability id u16) is written by only four direct stores (BattleAction_BuildUnitRequest 0x1402832AD, sub_1402831D8 0x140283235, Formula_37_RendEquipment 0x140307EB9 and its restore 0x140307EED); every other copy of it goes through Mem_CopyChecked with size 0x14.

notes: Source: IDA reads of 2026-11-12.

name: BattleCommandMenuStates
scope: battle, own turn: command menu, Abilities list, Move tile selection, target selection, facing prompt
summary: How to tell the screens of an own battle turn apart and which row the command menu cursor is on, from game state only: the glove position, the focused widget and the text of the instruction-message widget.

behavior.text: the main command menu is up while the radio-menu entry count at UIAddonFFTOBattleCommand +856 is above 0 (5 entries: Move, Abilities, Wait, Status, Auto-Battle); the count stays 5 while the Abilities list is open and is 0 on tile, target and facing screens.

the finger cursor (glove, node CursorRef) sits at x 1158 for the main column with y 760, 814, 871, 928, 983 for rows 0 to 4 (about 55.8 apart, +-2 from the bob); in the Abilities list it sits at x 1278 with y 759 for the first entry (Attack), 814 for the next.

the selected (+1120) and hover (+1124) row fields read -1 until the cursor first moves, and read -1 again after returning from any sub-screen, while the glove stays on the row the sub-screen was opened from. They are therefore not a reliable row; the glove y is.

the cursor is remembered across cancels: B from the facing prompt returns to row 2 (Wait), B from tile selection returns to row 0, B from the Abilities list returns to row 1, B from target selection returns to the Abilities list on its first entry.

the Abilities list is drawn inside the command widget (ffto_battle_command.uib stays the focused widget, glove x 1278); Attack opens target selection; the job command (Martial Arts for a Monk with nothing learnt) did nothing on A.

tile selection, target selection and the facing prompt have no focused widget (empty focus), no glove, the same set of visible screens and the same agents; they differ only by the text of the Title node under TextBoardInstructionMessage in ffto_battle_menu_instruction_message_02.uib, which is drawn (draw gate set) only while a prompt is up: 'Select a tile and press [A] to move.', 'Select a target and press [A] to confirm.', 'Select a facing direction and press [A] to confirm.' ([A] stands for button-glyph characters in the private-use area).
the node's text stays set after the prompt is gone; only the draw gate (node +204 != 0 and +145 == 0) says it is shown.

A on Wait opens the facing prompt; A there ends the turn and writes the battle autosave; B returns to the menu. A on Status (row 3) opens ffto_status_ver03.uib and B returns to the menu with the glove on row 3.

the battle map is 13 x 13 here (bytes at 0x140C6AD6A / 0x140C6AD6B); the 8-byte tile records at 0x140D8DCB0 are row-major (index = y * 13 + x), flag byte +5. In Move tile selection bit 0x20 marks the lit tiles the unit can stop on (3 tiles for a boxed-in Chemist, matching the screen) and bit 0x40 marked the three allies it could pass; units cannot pass enemies. A on an unlit tile shows ffto_common_error.uib with 'Select a tile within movement range.' and changes nothing. A on a lit tile moves the unit (+79/+80 of its unit record change), returns to the command menu with the cursor on Abilities.

the cursor starts on the unit's own tile and moves one tile per pad direction press, relative to the camera. RB / LB rotate the camera by quarter turns, so UP / RIGHT are not fixed compass directions (seen: RIGHT = +x with UP = +y, then RIGHT = +y with UP = -x after RB). The tile table gives each tile's height (record byte +2, byte +3 = half step) and the HUD node TextHeight shows the height of the tile under the cursor, so one press plus the table tells the current mapping.

the cursor's own tile and the camera rotation were not found in memory (not in the tile table; the camera manager at 0x143CDA758 and 512 KB of globals from 0x143C80000 showed no change under RB). The debugger does not need them: it measures the mapping from the heights.

an attack is four steps: Abilities, Attack, target tile, then a preview screen (no prompt line; footer Cancel / Confirm / Move Viewpoint) where A executes it and B returns to target selection with the cursor still on the chosen tile. A on a target out of range shows an error and stays. While the target prompt is up the tile table at 0x140D8DCB0 still holds the last Move range, so the attack range lives elsewhere (not found). The menu returns about 3 s after Confirm; the target can counter.

the battle can show modal tutorial / message pages (a KO turning into a chest; Next then Done) that hold the turn until A is pressed per page, and the Game Over screen (ffto_battle_gameover_02.uib) whose entries Retry, Load, Return to World Map, Return to Title Screen appear after a first pad press shows the glove.

in target selection the game marks tiles yellow (in range and targetable, empty or occupied), white (outside the x/y range) and red with a slash (inside the x/y range but out of vertical reach); a normal sword attack reaches the four tiles around the unit. The tile table at 0x140D8DCB0 keeps the Move range while targeting; the marks are in the range-mark array (next record).

the yellow (targetable) tiles are the records whose byte 0 is non-zero in the range-mark array at 0x1418004E0 (512 records of 5 bytes, index = x + y * width + layer * 256, layer = the acting unit's z bit, unit +81 >> 7), written by BattleRange_MarkRing (via sub_14027F974 for ability ranges, sub_14027F5B4 / sub_14027FD2C / sub_14027F270 for the other command kinds). Brice at (6,1) with a sword: byte 0 set at (6,0), (5,1), (6,2), clear at (7,1) (too high), matching the screen.

notes: The debugger reads the prompt by a scoped text scan (0.45 s once, then the single node by address). The game's own state variable that selects the prompt was not looked for; this is an observation, not the engine's rule.
open_questions: ? The engine field behind the prompt (a UI state or the battle action mode). ? Meaning of range-mark bytes 1 to 4 and of values above 1 in byte 0. ? Whether Move shows a different prompt when the unit has no reachable tile. ? Where the cursor tile and the camera rotation live. ? The job command's ability list for a unit that has learnt abilities.

name: BattleEffectsAreOneFilePerNumber
summary: A battle effect is one self-contained file per effect number (0..511): EffectFile_GetTrackRow gives its pack file and size, the loader reads it into one shared buffer and the effect runs from offsets inside the file.

behavior.text: Effect_SelectForAbility masks the number to 0x1FF; the file table, the 512-entry base pointer array and the NXD readers are the only per-number data outside the file; no stock effect word yields 511 (its file row is empty) and the five hard-coded number tests (33..36, 65, 71, 73, 230, 242, 451, 464, 485) never see it.

BattleAct_SetupEffect is called only from BattleAct_Step, which first calls BattleAct_BuildResult with the slot byte +0x1BC of the scene object's unit (+0x148); that function reads the action's ability word at g_BattleUnitTable + slot * 0x200 + 0x1A2; rdi still holds the scene object at the call to Effect_SelectForAbility (0x140206317).

EffectNxd_LoadRow writes its effect argument to the renderer slot +88 and nothing reads that field back (two writers, no reader by its displacement 0x24418 from g_CharaRenderer); the flag readers and Effect_TintByNxdScale take the key from their argument or word_141D330BC.

open_questions: ? the blocks between an effect file's header and its texture section are not decoded.

name: BattleEntryDataIsFiveFilesByKey
summary: The entry key (variable 50) selects 16 entries of 40 bytes: keys 1..127 read from file 224, 128..255 from 225, 256..383 from 226, 384..511 from 227 (81,920 bytes each, 128 keys), and keys 512..591 from file 892 (51,200 bytes, 80 keys); the block address has no bound.

behavior.text: TextKind25_LoadPool allocates 0x14000 bytes and reads 81,920 bytes of file 224 + (key div 128) for keys below 512, and allocates 0xC800 bytes and reads 51,200 bytes of file 892 for keys of 512 and above.

Battle_GetEntryBlock returns the loaded base + 640 x index, with the index the key reduced below 128 (or the key minus 512); there is no comparison with the file's key count, so key 592 or more addresses memory past the buffer.
key 0 means no entries.
the OverrideEntryData rows are looked up with the same key (and index 0..15) and overwrite the entries in place.
the entry tiles are absolute map coordinates; no table maps an entry key to a map id.

notes: The entry keys of the stock scenario records reach 585; the random formations are below 229.
open_questions: ? the offsets of the tile and facing bytes inside the 40-byte entry.

name: BattleFaceIsThePoolSpriteByte
summary: A battle unit's face is not a portrait code: the look pool's sprite byte is stored as the pool's face value and ten readers use it as the face number behind the 0xCD cap; a separate code exists only for one special unit.

behavior.text: sub_14026E838 stores the scene unit's byte +0xA into g_LookPoolFaceValue[pool index] in both branches; sub_140210AF0 clears the ten dwords to -1; Battle_SaveCapture and Battle_RestoreCapture copy them (sub_140304BEC).

readers: sub_1401F3858, sub_140214134, TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel, TurnPanel_SetTag, Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt and sub_1402DF374 take it as the face when the unit's code is -1 and cap it at 0xCD (above: -1); sub_140221798 returns it; sub_14021FA50 hands it raw to the dialogue slot writer; sub_140338A28 and sub_1403980AC write it to g_DialogueFaceSlot0 and g_HdFaceSlotValues.

the code comes from sub_14022AA88 only for a unit whose +401 equals byte_140C6AD76 (code byte_140C6AD7A); the 0x9F guards of five readers (0x140214188, 0x1402150B4, 0x14021569D, 0x14022994C, 0x1402E0556) test that code, never the pool value.
so in battle numbering a stock look's face number is its sprite number (0..169); a sprite of 170..205 would draw the stock face of that number and 206..254 no face.

the battle portraits are UI faces (FaceTexture_FormatName, the same wldface part files as the menus), not g2d entries: the active-unit panel through Battle_UnitStatusFill -> sub_140214134(slot, colour), the turn order through TurnPanel_SetTag's inline copy (face in ebx after the cap at 0x1402157A0, slot in r13), the panel of a unit under the cursor through Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt's inline copy (face in r11d and edx at 0x140229A5E, slot = word +0xA of argument 4 saved at rsp+0x6C; sub_1402DF374 the same at 0x1402E0668), TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel's at 0x1402151B3 (edi; slot saved at rsp+0xB0).
the store indexes the ten dwords by the pool index, which runs to 14: pools 10..14 store past the table (0x1437A5A08..0x1437A5A18).

name: BattleForkDeterminism
scope: a battle resumed from one autosave and driven by the same scripted input in two runs
summary: A battle can be forked only at a save point: the autosave restores the world work copy and a battle image, but not the random stream, the frame counters, the input state or the thread/GPU state. The recipe forces the shared random state after the battle is up and then drives both runs with the same one-input-then-read-state script.

behavior.text: `SaveSlot_WriteFromLive` packs the live state into `g_SaveWorkCurrent` (40164 bytes) and, when the situation byte is 1, queues a `resume_enma%02d_world.sav` entry; `SaveSlot_LoadToLive` loads that entry and flags a battle resume.
the autosave PNG holds the resume entries, not a `fftsave.bin` slot image; the world entry embeds a work copy at +356.
the random state is the four dwords at 0x1408E5FC8; `Rng_Percent` and many inlined copies step it with shifts 11 and 8.
the state is written from a scaled `Time_GetTimestamp` value at 0x1401E72F9, inside the scene setup function `sub_1401E6E5C`.
no save function references the state; the state is not in the 40164-byte work copy.
therefore two cold loads of the same autosave start with different random streams; writing the same 16 bytes after the battle scene is up gives both runs the same stream for every draw that follows.

the turn engine ticks CT once per `Battle_TurnEngine` call (phase 0), and that call happens per frame; a wall-clock input delay can therefore change the number of CT ticks between two otherwise identical presses.
`Time_GetTimestamp` reads the clock provider at 0x143CD9BC8 and returns 1/300000-second units; `App_RunFrame` uses it for the 1/60-second frame limiter.
the game samples input per frame, so the same input sequence does not guarantee the same frame alignment.
event tasks run on their own OS threads (`EventThread_Yield`); the battle turn engine runs in the game thread.
event scripts can interleave differently with the battle loop, but they do not own the battle random state.
whether the 1.07 MB main/attack/fturn images contain a copy of the random state, the camera record or the frame counters; the scene setup writes a fresh seed, so a stored copy would not be restored.
whether loading an autosave rewrites the autosave file; a byte copy of the PNG before branch A and a restore before branch B is the safe recipe.

open_questions: ? Which autosave descriptor is the battle save (the Load Game list order is the only offline clue); ? the lifetime of the seeded state when the battle scene is rebuilt; ? the effect of the UI frame generator on battle presentation traces.

name: BattleHudAndUnitFields
scope: the Jobs screen and a battle's first turn
summary: What the game shows from the Jobs screen into a battle, as seen live.

behavior.text: in the Siedge Weald battle Ramza's battle unit (unit table slot 16) has job byte 76 (0x4C), the Knight job. The battle HUD names his job 'Knight' with the Knight icon, Lv. 8 and 3004 JP, which is the Knight job's progress. HP is 77/77, MP 12/12.

the command menu is Move, Abilities, Wait, Status, Auto-battle; the Abilities list has Attack (description 'Attacks with the equipped weapon, or bare fists if no weapon is equipped.', under a Knight heading). The move range was 54 tiles from tile (3, 5).

name: BattleMapIdPathsAndTheirWidths
summary: The battle map id travels as a 32-bit global (0x140D3A838) set from scene variable 51 or from one of two signed 16-bit event words (-1 means none); the current-map global used for resources is another 32-bit global (0x140784478); the battle save header keeps the id in ONE byte.

behavior.text: the battle load passes the 32-bit global (or scene variable 51) to the map task, which stores it into the 32-bit current-map global before calling the map loader (whose argument is 16 bits).

two event words (0x140D40924, 0x140D40928) are compared with -1 and sign-extended when they set the global; the instruction that writes them from script data was not read, so their operand width is ?.
SceneVar_Read returns a 32-bit value and SceneVar_Write takes a 32-bit value; the width of the stored cell behind them was not read (?).

SaveHeader_FillBattleFields stores the low byte of the battle map id at +0x2C of the save header; I: it is for display in the save list; ? the reader of that byte was not found, and whether it also steers a resume.
the battle capture (SceneUnits_SaveRestore) copies the 32-bit global whole.

every other reader found of the two globals compares the id with stock map numbers (6, 8, 14, 15, 22, 23, 26, 33, 50, 52, 53 to 83, 62, 64, 82, 92, 94, 127 appear) or searches a short fixed list keyed by it (five entries); none indexes an array by it other than the tables above, and an id with no match takes the default branch.
one function writes the sentinel 0x77777777 into the current-map global as 'no map'.

notes: Together with MoveFindTakenBitsAreFourPerMapInA128ByteArray this is why map ids above 255 are not safe in this build.

name: BattleMotionNumbers
summary: A battle action names its animation by a motion number from two tables (one per ability, one per weapon type); the unit stores motion + 1, and the motion number is the pair index of the classic animation file (front view at twice the number, back view one more).

behavior.text: the ability table (3 bytes an ability, at 0x140672DA0) holds the charge type, the motion number and the battle text number; motion 0 means a plain weapon attack, motion 1 a ranged special that becomes motion 58 when the target is adjacent or on the same tile, and every other value is used as it stands.
the weapon table (3 bytes a weapon animation type, 24 types, at 0x140673890) holds three motion numbers per type; types 19 to 23 hold none.
BattleAnim_StartMotion stores motion + 1 as the unit's animation number (scene object +0x10).

animation pointer 2 x motion (front) and 2 x motion + 1 (back) in the classic animation file lands the motions of every weapon type that has any on animations that draw the attack frames (frame numbers 84 and up) and carry the hit-marker opcode, with one exception that carries none (a weapon type whose animations do not mark the hit). Of the 57 distinct motion values in the ability table, 34 were tested: the values from 40 up land on animations that draw action frames; the low values (0, 1, 22, 34, 36) land on single-frame poses and one value (112) on a pointer with no frames. Other offsets (motion, motion + 1, 2 x motion - 26) land on movement poses and unrelated animations; 2 x motion + 2 lands on the next animation of the same group, so the choice of 2 x motion rests on the ordering of the weapon triples (see the next bullet). The code that does this conversion was not located.

the three motions of a weapon type are three variants of one attack in the order high, middle, low of the target's height: the one weapon type read in code (type 12) picks its motion from a signed angle word, the first below -682, the second from -682 to 682, the third above 682.

because the movement tables (CharAnimSeq) only hold animation ids 1 to 73 and the motions used in battle reach 118 (animation 236), the attack and cast animations are read from the classic animation file, not from those tables.

notes: The 17 frames past 181 of the robed layout (frames 182 to 198, four pieces each, all with art in every sheet of that layout) are drawn by no classic animation; what draws them is unknown.
open_questions: ? the function that reads the +0x10 number each frame; ? the scene mode values 457 and 292 tested by BattleAnim_StartMotion; ? what draws the robed layout's frames 182 to 198.

name: BattlePaletteSourceByLookRange
summary: Where a battle unit's palette row comes from depends on its sprite number: the generic looks (96..133) and 159..162 take the unit's byte +4, every other look its CharShape row's colour override or the queue palette.

behavior.text: SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry tests the sprite word against 159, 160, 161, 162 and sprite - 0x60 <= 0x25; those take unit byte +4 (the queue's palette word when there is no unit) with a limit of 5.

name: BattlePanelJobLineShowsDashesAtLevelZero
summary: The job line of a battle unit panel shows 'Lv. --' and '--' for JP and next whenever the job record's level is 0. The record is built from copies of the unit's level and JP arrays: BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord copies them into its own stack frame and JobRecord_FromJobId reads the copies; BattleMain_SetPanelJobRecord stores the result for the panel.

behavior.text: UnitPanel_FillJobLine tests the level (record +68) first; at 0 or less every number of the line is replaced by the dash text.

moving the cursor onto a unit called JobRecord_FromJobId from BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord with the frame copies of the arrays, then BattleMain_SetPanelJobRecord from Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt with that record.
monsters (all job level nibbles 0) show the dashes.

every generic job of a spawned human unit starts at level 1 or more (UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord) with 100..199 JP (Unit_InitJobJp), and level 1 needs 100 JP on the stock curve, so a human unit's own job never shows the dashes.

behavior.text: BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord (from Battle_UnitStatusFill, Battle_TimelineRefresh, Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt and sub_1402DF374) builds the panel's job record from byte +3 (0x1400FCFC9) and frame copies of the level, JP and total JP arrays.

name: BattleRosterCopiesCarryTheBattleSlotAt44
summary: In battle the party records are copies of battle unit records: PartyUnit_FillFromWorkRecord fills the battle roster records from the battle unit table, writing the unit's battle slot at +44 and its save slot at +0x1E, and UnitWork_BuildForSlot (battle modes 101 and 104) copies the roster into the party records with one memmove, so there +44 is a battle slot, not the save slot it names outside battle.

behavior.text: PartyUnit_FillFromWorkRecord stores work +2 at +0x1E, work +1 at +0x22 and again at +0x2C (44), and the work record's job byte (+3) as the job word (+0x24).

UnitWork_BuildForSlot in modes 101 / 104 calls the roster builder (sub_140360780, which fills one 640-byte record per standing unit from the battle unit table) and copies the records whole into the party record array, then points the party pointer table at them.
party record 8 held +44 = 16 and +0x1E = 0 for the unit of battle slot 16 whose save slot is 0; save slot 16 was empty.

name: BattleTextOverlaysAndPreview
scope: battle: event dialogue, notice banner, attack / item preview, deployment placement
summary: Where the battle's dialogue, notices and action preview are drawn, how placement works, and what the preview numbers meant in play, as seen live.

behavior.text: event dialogue is drawn in ffto_event.uib, which never takes the focus (the sortie screen keeps it through the battle opening): node Title holds the speaker, node Text the line. Two balloons can be drawn at once (the previous one stays while the next opens); A advances one box, with a moment between boxes where none is drawn.

the red notice banner is ffto_common_error.uib, node Title, also never focused; it read 'Unable to use. The unit either lacks any usable abilities or does not meet their requirements.' when a Monk with no learned Martial Arts chose that command, and faded within a few seconds while the list stayed closed.

the action preview (ffto_battle_main_ver04.uib) has node TextHit = hit chance, TextDamage = the damage, or the recovery for an item, TextHPNum = actor and target HP, and a second percentage in node Textmatch. Nine previews in one battle matched the result exactly when the action landed; a Potion's 'Recovery 30' was capped at the target's max HP (41/53 to 53, 24/51 to 51).

the hit chance depends on the side attacked from: a Bomb facing -y (unit +0x51 = 0) showed 80 % from its front tile and 100 % from its side tile; the 80 % attack missed, the side attack landed. Earlier front attacks showed 62 % and 82 %.

Textmatch varied by attacker and target pair (75 % for a Knight against a Black Goblin and 100 % against a Bomb; 75 % for a Monk against a Goblin and a Bomb), which fits a zodiac compatibility figure; not checked against the zodiac table.
a Chemist's Potion can target any tile within 4 (a full diamond of radius 4).

deployment: after a unit is placed, the tile cursor moves to a free tile by itself and the unit carousel opens on the next unit not yet placed; placing the last free member opens 'Commence battle? Yes / No' by itself. From the second placement on, the sortie screen holds the focus with no glove; before the first it has no focus.
A on a battleground first shows the location's name on black while the battle loads; units are already in the battle table, no unit has the turn (slot 0xFFFFFFFF); deployment follows by itself.

the footer (ffto_footer_02.uib) keeps hidden labels of the previous footer in its tree (e.g. 'Commence Battle' through the first turns): only labels visible up their node chain are on screen. While an action of the player's side plays, the footer is hidden.
the camera turns by itself between turns and phases (yaws 0x200, 0x600, 0xA00, 0xE00 seen), and pad directions for the tile cursor and the facing prompt follow it.

notes: The preview and dialogue layouts are the game's own. Read with the project debugger (state reads and the UI text scanner).

name: BlendFactorUsesStoredSourceAlpha
scope: GPU (the test machine's GPU and driver), UI draws into an 8-bit target
summary: The destination factor of a UI draw's blend (1 - source alpha) uses the source alpha as the 8-bit target stores it: result = round(source) + round(destination * (1 - round8(source alpha))), with round8 = the target's UNORM store.

behavior.basis: (frame t4, the two black edge fades JobTree/BG/Rect00 and Rect01, alpha interpolated from 255 to 0 across 266.7 px over the floor)
behavior.text: solving each screen column for the multiplier that reproduces the capture, the float alpha is outside the feasible range in 16 of 61 columns (left) and 10 of 43 (right); the alpha stored to 8 bits first in 4 and 4. Linear quantisations of the interpolated value (1/256, 1/512, 1/1024, half floats, truncation) all fit worse.
frame t4 goes from 97.2 % to 97.9 % of pixels exact (chips 0.082 -> 0.037, ring box 0.124 -> 0.093, every region equal or better); the generic-male sweep frame from 96.9 % to 97.8 %.
D3D lets the blend unit work at the render target's precision, which converts the shader's outputs to the format before blending; this record only states what the frames show.

open_questions: ? the remaining misses under the edge fades. V (2026-10-31, live: the Job Tree captured with JobTree/BG/Rect00 and Rect01 at opacity 0 and at 1, so the game's own floor under them is known): they are not in the floor; in the columns whose alpha x 255 has a fraction from about 0.5 to 0.8 the game stores one level less than the rounded exact alpha, over a vertical stretch that is longest at mid height (the game's interpolated alpha lies up to about 0.3 / 255 below the exact value and changes smoothly with y). I: the GPU's attribute interpolation precision; not modelled (it would be a fit).

name: BlendTermsRoundedSeparately
scope: GPU (the test machine's GPU and driver), UI draws into a layer target
summary: A UI draw's blend into its 8-bit target behaves as if both terms were rounded to 8 bits before they are added: result = round(source) + round(destination * (1 - source alpha)), not round(source + destination * (1 - source alpha)).

behavior.basis: (frame t4, the floor: a solid rect (13, 12, 11)
behavior.text: under the stone texture at alpha 50 / 255): the separate rounding reproduces 97.9 % of 389043 floor pixels exactly, one rounding 28.3 %. The destination term alone explains the game's integer offsets 10 / 10 / 9 (13, 12, 11 x 205 / 255 rounded).

the same result comes from drawing the textured node into its own 8-bit layer and compositing it (store 1 then store 2); the two cannot be told apart on this frame. On the glove (drawn into a cleared target) both rules agree with the measured 99.4 %.

behavior.basis: (studio, GameCompose.draw with this rule and the truncated vertex alpha)
behavior.text: the whole frame t4 goes from 43.8 % to 93.3 % of pixels exact (header 99.9 %, floor 92.6 - 94 %).

name: CharShapeKeyByteSites

name: CharShapeRowMissingFaultsTheFormation
summary: The battle formation code reads a CharShape row (NXD 174) keyed by the scene unit's sprite byte and, on one path, reads the row's byte +0x2C with no row: a sprite number without a CharShape row faults.

behavior.text: sub_140216EB4 (from sub_140213F14) loads the key from the scene unit's +0xA (0x14021708E), looks the row up through NxdRegistry_Find(0xAE) and NxdTable_GetRowById, and when the entry is null sets the row pointer to 0 (0x140217157) before reading +0x2C at 0x140217172.
NxdTable_GetRowById checks the key against the table's minimum and maximum, then indexes densely or searches; it has 474 references.

the CharShape row is 48 bytes in column order (DLCFlags +0, comment string offset +4, ids +8..+36, bytes +40..+47, Height at +44): the offsets the readers use (+8, +12, +16, +20..+32, +44, +45, +46) match.

an entry whose first qword is negative stands for the static default row at 0x1406F5ED0 (CharShape_ApplyClut, SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry), so 'a row of its own' is an entry with a non-negative first qword and a non-null NxdEntry_GetRow.

name: CharShapeRowsANewLookNeeds
scope: engine (sprite rows in the NXD data)
summary: The CharShape rows (NXD table 174, keyed by look number) end at key 158 and twelve functions look a look up there.

behavior.text: CharaRender_LookupLutParams (menu renderer: shadow size and LUT region rows) takes the key as an unsigned 32-bit value; CharShape_ApplyClut (the palette colour override, called by CharaPalette_LoadClassic on the menu path) takes it as a byte, so a look of 256 or more reaches it truncated.
a missing row is a null return in every lookup; sub_140216EB4 (battle formation) turns a null entry into a null row pointer and then reads byte +0x2C of it (0x140217172), a fault.

name: CheckpointCopyHoldsTheLiveUnitRecords
scope: the checkpoint copy of the slot record (g_SaveCheckpointCopy)
summary: The checkpoint writer packs the party into the work copy, copies the work copy to the checkpoint copy, and then overwrites the checkpoint copy's unit area with the live unit records. Whatever the pack step put in the unit area of the work copy is therefore not in the checkpoint copy; the checkpoint holds the live records.

behavior.text: sub_1402CEEE8 fills g_SaveWorkCurrent with 0xFF, calls UnitWork_BuildForSlot(0) and SaveWork_PackFromParty(0), and copies the 0x9CE4 bytes to g_SaveCheckpointCopy.

it then copies 0x7E90 bytes (54 unit records of 600) from g_UnitSaveData to 0x142E80968, which is g_SaveCheckpointCopy + 0x518; the pack code writes the units at work copy + 1304 = 0x518, so the live records land exactly on the unit area of the checkpoint's slot record and replace what the pack put there.

the same function also copies many other live fields (item stores, event variables, world state, flags) into the checkpoint block, so the checkpoint block is a mix of the packed slot record and live fields.

the restore twin sub_1402CF768 (after sub_140246014 with restore = 1 has copied the checkpoint to the work copy) copies the checkpoint's unit area back to g_UnitSaveData with one 0x7E90-byte move, so the live records survive a checkpoint round trip as they were, and the work copy's own unit area is not what is restored.
sub_140246014 with restore = 0 would pack and store without the live-record copy, but its only direct caller passes restore = 1.

consequence: a change to job bytes or spare bytes in the work copy's unit area (after SaveWork_PackFromLive / SaveWork_PackFromParty) reaches slot saves written from the work copy, but not the checkpoint copy built by sub_1402CEEE8; data that must survive through the checkpoint must be in the live records (g_UnitSaveData).

sub_1402CEEE8 is called by sub_1402B8690, which has thirteen callers in the event and scene code; the checkpoint is captured from scene paths, not from a save-menu action (the trigger of each caller was not read).

notes: Evidence: IDA, sub_1402CEEE8, sub_140246014, sub_1402CF768 and SaveWork_PackFromLive read in full on 2026-11-09.
open_questions: ? which caller of sub_1402B8690 captures the checkpoint at a battle autosave; ? whether the 0x7E90 copy also runs on any path that does not go through sub_1402CEEE8.

name: ClassicSpriteFilesByNumber
scope: the sprite pack, classic palettes and portraits of stock shapes
summary: Classic sprite files are numbered entries of fftpack.bin, and the `offset` column of the classic kind tables is that file number; the game has no portrait for shapes 56 and 57.

behavior.text: `system/ffto/fftpack.bin` (the English pack `fftpack.en.bin`, 213,143,552 bytes inflated) has header dwords 3931 (file count), 16, 15740, 32768, then 3931 byte offsets and 3931 sizes (offsets in bytes, not sectors). The game's pack 0002 also holds named copies of 178 `fftpack/unit/*.bin` files; each tested named copy is byte-identical to exactly one fftpack entry: `battle_dami_spr.bin` = file 91 (44,690 bytes), `battle_kasanek_spr.bin` = 130 (40,516), `battle_mina_m_spr.bin` = 140 (43,433; the Squire's, found by pixels).

the `offset` column of `exe.sprite.classic_kind` / `classic_kind2` is this file number (the first argument of GameData_ReadSectors); stock shapes 93 and 94 use files 91 and 130, shape 56 uses 152, shape 57 uses 140, both through both tables.
`exe.sprite.hd_entry_by_shape`: shape 56 -> g2d entry 922, shape 57 -> 924 (each shape's second sheet is the next entry); shapes 159..169 -> 1110, 1112 .. 1130.

the game's packs hold no `wldface_056_*` or `wldface_057_*` portrait; `wldface_058_08` exists. The four portrait code tables hold 0 for shapes 55, 56, 57, 93, 94; `exe.sprite.scene_shape` (sprite id 0..159 -> shape) maps no id to shape 56 or 57 (id 141 -> 58). I: so no portrait code gives a unit of look 56 / 57 the face 56 / 57 through the stock path.

a party unit's save record (`g_UnitSaveData` + 600 n, byte +0) set to a value below 0x80 makes the roster draw that look: look 56 showed the art of g2d entry 922 with the colours of classic file 152, and Ramza's portrait (code 0).

a classic sprite file's 4-bpp pixels (after its 0x200-byte palette, 256 pixels a row) and its HD sheet (512 a row) share colour indices at double size: sampled every 3 pixels, a sheet and its own classic file agree on 73 % and 76 % of the classic file's non-transparent pixels (the two test pairs), unrelated pairs on 2 % to 13 %.
the pack index of the game's packs records a CRC and a size per file (`fftpack.en.bin`: size 0x0CB45000, the uncompressed size), readable without inflating the file.
the face number is formatted into the texture name unchanged at four digits: a face number 9056 resolved to `wldface_9056_08`.

name: CombatSetJobBytesAreOnlyCopied
summary: The three combat-set job bytes of a unit record (party record +462, +550, +638; save record +380, +468, +556) are never read as a job by the status, equipment or combat-set screens: every access seen is a whole-record copy or clear.

name: CursorDrawnThroughLayerTarget
summary: The glove reaches the screen in two 8-bit stores: it is drawn into a cleared layer target (premultiplied, rounded) and that layer is then blended onto the frame (dst = layer + dst * (1 - layer alpha), rounded again).

behavior.text: one store reproduces 76.3 % of the glove's changed values (max 2), two stores 93.3 % (max 1) and with the 1/256 snapping and weights 99.4 %.

every widget root is a layer (WidgetRootsAreLayers), so the glove, which has no effect of its own, goes through the layer path like all other UI: its draws land in RT 26 (cleared to (0, 0, 0, 0) per atlas page, blend ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA) and the layer is then composited onto the frame target by a shader read-modify-write (LayerBlitOverFrameTarget). The general rule and its order are in the flow UiLayerComposite and the behavior LayerCompositeOrder.
the formulas are in LayerContentDrawnIntoCleared8BitTarget (store 1) and LayerBlitOverFrameTarget (store 2).

name: CursorGloveBob
scope: finger cursor (the glove on the Job Tree)
summary: The glove's idle bob: a 40-frame, looping, position track on the IconHand node of the Hand component, played on the UI frame time, sampled as an integer, and added to the glove's glide only in the node matrices. This record gives the rule exactly (decoded from the code and the two cursor UIB files).

behavior.text: the Hand component's Loop state is 40 frames; its IconHand position track has keys at frame 0 (0, -2) curve id 20 (OutSine), frame 20 (-20, -2) curve id 19 (InSine) and frame 40 (0, -2) curve id 2 (the file stores interpolation ids 19, 18 and 1). A second track (tag 5031) is a jump marker from frame 40 to frame 0.

the Widget component of ffto_finger_cursor.uib has its own Loop state of 40 frames whose only track links frames 0 to 40 to state Loop of the CursorRef node (the Hand): frame 0 -> child frame 0, frame 40 -> child frame 40.

sampling at the Hand's frame f (a float): the key is the last one with frame <= (int)f; u = (f - key frame) / (next frame - key frame) in single precision; for f < 20: x = trunc(fl(fl(-20 * sin((u*pi)*0.5)) + 0)) with u = f / 20; for 20 <= f < 40: x = trunc(fl(fl(20 * (1 - cos((u*pi)*0.5))) + (-20))) with u = (f - 20) / 20; y = trunc(-2) = -2. trunc is the conversion toward zero, so x is an integer from -20 to 0 and sits at or to the right of the continuous value (for example frame 1: -1.569 -> -1).

IconHand's position is the sampled pair (absolute state). Its local matrix is translation (pivot + position) - 0.8 * pivot with the node's pivot (100, 20) and scale 0.8, so the glove's top-left in the 1920 x 1080 layout space is glide + (-86, -17) + (x, y) + (20, 4) (pivot * (1 - 0.8)), then the layer transform. The glide position (an integer from roundf) and the bob (an integer from truncation) are summed in float matrices; nothing rounds the sum.
the bob is in layout pixels (not scaled by the glove's 0.8); the screen scale applies afterwards like for every UI pixel.
the phase is the main component's Loop frame. It is advanced once per UI frame by dt (see UIStateClock) and wrapped by the loop at frame >= 40: frame and time become 0, the overshoot is dropped.

restart (phase 0) happens on every UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop, called by UIAgentCursor_Show and UIAddonFingerCursor_ResetPose; the Loop stops (and later restarts at 0) on UIAgentCursor_Hide, UIAddonFingerCursor_SetPose / FreezePose and static mode. Moving the glove (glide, arrival, retarget, hiding the node for lack of a target) does not touch the clock.
none of the Job Tree addon's functions refers directly to the cursor functions (decompile text search).
so panel-to-panel cursor moves inside the Job Tree do not restart the bob; a call through a helper was not excluded.

behavior.basis: (computed from the decoded rule in single precision, not read from the game)
behavior.text: with dt of exactly 1/60 s the frame at the k-th tick after a restart is k for k = 1 .. 39 and 0 at the 40th (the loop sets it to 0 because 40.0 >= 40), so the displayed frame sequence is 1, 2, ..., 39, 0, 1, ...; the x sequence is 0 at frame 0, then -1, -3, -4, -6, -7, -9, -10, -11, -12, -14, ... down to -20 at frame 20 and back up symmetrically. With dt between 5000 and 5100 ticks of 1/300000 s the cycle is still 40 ticks (frames k * dt * 60); at 4999 ticks it would be 41.
after a restart the first applied frame is about 1 (GUINode_PlayState applies nothing; the next update advances first).

behavior.basis: (live, 2026-10-30, 12 phases from 0 to 39 with the clock frozen)
behavior.text: IconHand's position read from the game equals this rule at every phase (0, -1, -7, -14, -18, -19, -20, -19, -18, -12, -4, -1 at frames 0, 1, 5, 10, 15, 19, 20, 21, 25, 31, 37, 39), and a viewer drawing the glove at glide + (-86, -17) + (20 + x, 4 - 2) on the game's own background reproduces the captured glove to within 2 levels (93 % of the pixels exact).

the main component's Loop runs (+0x69 = 1) with the loop byte set (+0x6C = 1) and range 0 .. 0 (so 0 .. 40); the Hand's Loop is paused (+0x6B = 1) and its frame is the main frame through the link's single-precision (f * 40) / 40 (31.363609 -> 31.363611). Writing rate 0 and a frame F into the main Loop held the clock at F (12 phases from 0 to 39 read back unchanged after a capture) and the captured glove moved between F = 0 and F = 20.

the bob does NOT restart when the Job Tree opens: with the main Loop held at frame 20 (rate 0) on the jobs list, X (Job Progress) opened the Job Tree and the same Loop state object still read rate 0, time 1/3, frame 20. The finger cursor is shared by the menus, so the phase on the Job Tree is whatever the clock had on the screen before.

notes: Rule for a viewer that reproduces the glove (what differs from a continuous sine): (1) take the phase f as the UI tick's frame, not as seconds * 60 wrapped by modulo; (2) x = the truncated value above, an integer; (3) y = -2; (4) top-left = glide origin + (-86 + x, -17 - 2) + (20, 4). The curve values are float32 results; only values within about 1e-5 of an integer could round differently from a double-precision evaluation.
open_questions: ? The frame timer's maximum step, which would shorten dt on a very slow frame.

name: EquipSessionFlagLifecycle
scope: the five party equipment words, the override array and the candidate array during an Outfitter or shop session
summary: Bit 15 marks a slot changed in the current session and priced into dword_143D1AC68; bit 14 is a list-entry 'cannot equip' mark. The commit strips bit 15 (and any bit 14) from every party word before the save is written; the cancel restores the override words.

behavior.text: the bit-15 writers are sub_140287D9C (four candidate words, 0x140288544), sub_1402D7280 (the unit word, 0x1402D733A) and the apply loops of sub_1402D5CC4 and sub_1402D6914, which copy a flagged candidate into the unit word.

the bit-15 readers treat the word as signed or compare it against 0x8000: sub_1402D58EC (0x1402D5A6C, 0x1402D5ACD), sub_1402D5FE4 (0x1402D6129 js), sub_1402D6464 (0x1402D6490), sub_1402D65D4 (0x1402D6621), sub_1402D5CC4 (0x1402D5EFA jns), sub_1402D6FB8 (0x1402D704C shr), sub_1402D7584 (0x1402D75E1 jge).
the bit-14 producers are Inventory_BuildEquipList (bts 0xE at 0x140288CAF) and Shop_BuildItemList (or 0x4000 at 0x140288FBD and 0x140289061); both write list entries, not party or candidate words.
sub_1402D7280 refuses a bit-14 candidate (bt 0xE at 0x1402D72A0), but the two apply loops test only bit 15 (0xFFFF8000), so a bit-14 candidate would be stored if one ever reached them.
after commit, sub_1402D65D4 masks every word at or above 0x4000 with 0x3FF and returns the override item to the inventory; bits 10..13 are not stripped but no writer sets them.

name: ErrandStateIsSpreadOverFiveStores
summary: An errand is an index 0..95 into five stores: its 23-byte record, a 4-bit state nibble in the event variables (864 + id), a delay byte, 9 bits of finish date and two new flags, plus the eight active slots that name it by a byte. The tavern board walks the 96 indices and lists those available in the current town.

behavior.text: the state nibble: 0x02 dispatched (Errand_Start, cleared by the result and the recall), 0x04 succeeded (Errand_ApplyResult at grade 0; Errand_IsAvailable's prerequisite), 0x08 set by Errand_Start.
the delay byte's low 6 bits are days before the errand is offered again: 0x60 after a grade 1 result, 0x90 after grade 2; one day = min(d, 32) - 1.
g_ErrandFinishDay holds 9 bits per errand (day 5, month 4): 96 x 9 bits are its 108 bytes.
bounds: 96 in the board and town loops, 160 nibbles (864..1023; 1024 and up trap), the slot's errand byte (255), the board entry's 11-bit id, 128 board entries, 8 slots.

name: EventIdRowOfTheCurrentEventIsReadWithoutANullTestWhenSkipping
summary: When the current event changes and skipping is enabled, EventScript_LoadCurrent looks up the EventId row (data table 156) of the event number and reads its byte +32 without testing the lookup result: an event number with no EventId row makes it read through a null pointer. The other readers of that table test for null.

behavior.text: EventScript_LoadCurrent compares scene variable 39 with the last loaded event; when they differ, the skip-flags word is not 1 and skipping is enabled, it takes the table (registry id 156), asks NxdTable_GetRowById for the event number, uses the default row for a negative entry, and otherwise sets the row pointer to null when the table or the row is missing, then reads byte +32 of it.
EventScript_Run (the dword at +28), sub_140254ABC (byte +39) and sub_14020261C (byte +37) read the same table for the current event and skip the read when the row is missing.

the event number is kept as a dword in the battle capture (Battle_SaveCapture stores scene variable 39 and the applier's resume key; Battle_RestoreSceneVars puts both back), the world save copies the whole scene variable store, and SaveSlot_WriteFromLive stores variable 39 as a 16-bit word at +284 of the slot record.

the other readers of variable 39 found (21 functions that load the index 39 directly) compare it with fixed event numbers or pass it on as a lookup key; none indexes an array by it except the per-event word table.

notes: I: byte +32 of the EventId row decides whether the skip check goes on to the fixed list of event numbers at 0x1407142E0 (read only as far as the branch).

name: EventSoundGroupAndMusicSlotOperandWidths
summary: The event sound group number reaches the player as a byte of a command record (class 44), as the replay of that byte from a word of the command state, or as the value of event variable 93 (a 32-bit cell); the music slot's sound id is stored in the low byte of a 16-bit word with the slot number in the high byte.

behavior.text: EventSoundGroup_Play widens its int argument with a sign extension and reads the byte at 4 x group - 4 + voice for the four voices, with no bound; group 0 therefore reads the four bytes before the table (in the stock image the high half of a data pointer) and a group above 56 reads whatever follows the table.

the class 44 command passes byte 9 of its record (0..255) and also stores it in the 16-bit word at 0x141862472 of the command state; the other writers of that word are class 45 (clears it) and class 47 (byte 9 or 0x4000), and the state restore function sub_1402F109C plays the word when it is nonzero unless bit 14 (0x4000) is set, which selects a UI dispatch with the bit removed. So the word never holds a group above 255: it replays the class 44 group.

EventCmd_ServiceRequests plays the value of event variable 93 when it is nonzero (variable 92 goes to another function, variable 94 sets the music slot); EventCmd_Run reads the three variables with EventVar_Read, which returns an unsigned 32-bit value.

event variables below 128 are whole 32-bit cells (EventVar_Alu stores a full dword for an index below 128; 128..863 are single bits, 864..1023 four-bit nibbles, 1024 and above end the task), so variable 93 can hold any 32-bit number; the ALU's add and multiply let a script build any value from a 16-bit operand. A value of 0x80000000 or more is a negative group after the conversion to int.

the class 32 command passes byte 9 of its record as the music sound id; the recorder stores it as (id or slot shifted left by 8) in a 16-bit word and the id again in a dword array indexed by the slot, so an id above 255 would overwrite the slot byte.
MusicSlot_FetchRecord reads three dwords at 3 x id from the music slot table, with an int id.

notes: A group above 255 is started only through event variable 93; the class 44 command, the state word and the UI dispatch carry at most a byte.
open_questions: ? which stock scripts write event variable 93, and whether any uses a group above 56.

name: FaceLookupInlineCopiesDisagreeAboveCode159
summary: The face-number lookup exists as SpriteId_ToShape and ten inline copies; for codes above 0x9F five of the copies answer differently from the function, so one table row cannot stand for all of them.

behavior.text: each copy compares the code with 0x9F (jump if above), reads g_SpriteIdToShape, else runs a switch over codes above 0x9F; the copies in sub_1401F3858, sub_140221798, sub_1402F8684, sub_140338A28 and sub_1403980AC give SpriteId_ToShape's answers for every code (unicorn, codes 160 to 1299).

Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt (0x140228778) and sub_1402DF374 use an older list: codes 184 to 187 give 192 down to 189, and codes 189 to 193, 196 to 201 and 205 give no face.

in each inline copy the fallback register is the -1 the function sets (an or with -1) before the copy (or the copy sets itself), the same register the code is compared with just before to skip an unset code.
the five copies that differ are battle HUD readers (turn panels, the status window)

name: FaceNumberCapsClipRawCodesToo
summary: Sixteen readers cap the face number at 0xCD (205): the twelve caps below and the four readers of the HD face table g_FaceG2dEntryByFace. Several caps also see a value that did not come from the face table.

behavior.text: at 0x14021FDEB (sub_14021FA50), 0x1402C0816 (Unit_GetSpriteSetId), 0x1402D7BE6 (sub_1402D7954) and 0x14032C469 (sub_14032B1A4) the mode word at 0x142FF9ED8 can skip SpriteId_ToShape, and the raw value is capped instead.

the four readers of g_FaceG2dEntryByFace (sub_14041AE44 at 0x14041B34E, sub_14041CAAC at 0x14041CC09, HdLayer_BindSheetTexture at 0x14041DA3F, sub_14041DAA4 at 0x14041DB82) each compare the slot value unsigned with 0xCD before the read; they belong to the same family.
in sub_140214134 and the two turn panel functions an unset code (-1) leaves the per-pool value from sub_14022AA88 in the capped register.
on the generic path of Unit_GetSpriteSetId (0x1402C086C) only a table answer is capped; an unmapped code is returned uncapped, and its bits 10 and 11 give the colour.
HdLayer_BindSheetTexture reads the face table at 0x140714EA0 with a limit of 0xCD for its first three texture ids.
