name: FastForwardState
scope: battle, event scripts (story scenes, battle dialogue) and the world map, enhanced edition
summary: How the fast-forward hold and the dialogue auto-advance toggle become state, how to read 'fast-forward is active now' from memory with no input, what gates a hold, and what the state changes.

behavior.text: recipe. gw = u64 at g_GlobalWork (0x143CD9DD0); level = u32 at gw + 0x58; mode = u32 at gw + 0x60; setting = u8 at (u64 at g_ConfigData 0x140C69690) + 0x37. Effective mode = 0 when setting is 1, or when setting is 2 and mode is 2; else mode. Fast-forward is active now when the effective mode is not 0 and level is 1 or 2; the game then runs 3 (level 1) or 5 (level 2) steps per displayed frame.

mode, written by the battle frame routine sub_140210AF0 every frame: in battle states 52 and 58 (an event script is running) mode = 2, or 0 while the event pause overlay is up (EventControl state 2); in every other state mode = 1 when g_FastForwardStateTable[g_BattleState] is non-zero, else mode = 0 and level = 0. The world map set-up writes mode 3; the battle control's destructor writes 0.
fast-forward is off in battle states 0, 4, 12, 21, 22, 23, 27, 31..36, 83, 84, 87, 88, 90, 91, 93 and 97, on in the other states up to 105.

battle (mode 1): level = 2 while action 90 is held, else 1 while action 89 is held, else 0, written every battle frame by BattleControl_FrameUpdate (enhanced edition, PauseManager byte +24 bit 4 clear, dword_140D3A840 == 0). A plain level test of the held byte: a button that is already down counts, there is no delay.

event script (mode 2), EventControl_RunningTick, once per displayed frame while the overlay state is 1: a press edge of action 89 or 90 is accepted only when the control's run timer (EventControl +0x28) has reached 0.75 s; it sets armed (+0x35). While armed and held (and +0x32 is 0) the hold timer +0x24 grows and the 'Fast-forwarding' label is shown (+0x2C = 1); when the hold timer reaches 1.0 s the level becomes 1 (2 with action 90 held). Releasing clears armed, the timer, the label and the level.

this is why a button held from before a scene never starts fast-forward (no press edge after the 0.75 s mark), why a fresh press shows the label at once, and why the first balloon advances about 1.2 s after the press (1.0 s ramp, then the page) and later ones faster (measured live 2026-11-09: label within 0.09 s, first advance about 1.2 s, later about 0.4 s).

EventControl_Reset zeroes both timers and the flags on every frame without an event tick, so the 0.75 s count restarts with each event script; EventControl_ApplyCarry restores a running fast-forward (armed, timer 1.0, level 1) at the start of a chained event whose EventId row has byte +35 set, and auto-advance when it has byte +34 set.

auto-advance: action 91 pressed toggles EventControl +0x2F (1 = on) when the event allows it; the dialogue window's auto indicator follows it. With the setting enableEventKeepAuto (config byte +0x3B) the latch g_EventKeepAutoLatch (u8 0x140C6AD73) switches it on again in the next event. It is not consulted while fast-forward is held.
world map (mode 3): level = 1 while action 89 is held (WorldMap_UpdateFastForward), cleared when a world panel opens.

what the level changes: GameTasks_RunFrameSteps repeats the whole task step 3 or 5 times per displayed frame and draws only the last; the UI animation time step is multiplied by the same number (UI_FrameUpdate); EventMessage_Task and EventMessage_Scripted stop waiting for a button on a finished page while the level is non-zero; the timed battle message closes after 180 / multiplier frames, not below 30 (sub_14020C30C); battle and event voices are not started (sub_1401EC958, EventVoice_PlayTask); the sound manager switches a state per level (sub_1401D6988).

predicted speed-up: frame-counted waits (animation, walking, effects, script waits) take 1/3 of the wall time at level 1 and 1/5 at level 2, as long as the machine can run the extra steps inside one frame; the text typing rate is also set from the multiplier (sub_14022280C passes it to the event window).
the pause overlays clear the level when they open (EventControl_TryOpenPause, MovieControl_TryOpenPause).

one more reader of action 89 outside these three handlers: the text-typing tick sub_1401E0688 (caller sub_1401DFB90) multiplies its time step by 4 while action 89 is held and dword_140D8DBA8 is not above 0; it never touches the level. ?: which screen that typed text belongs to (the UI object at +248 of the UI root).
no code that draws a fast-forward indicator in battle outside dialogue was found; the only label is the dialogue window's node.

notes: Buttons: action 89 = Ctrl, fifth mouse button, pad RB; action 90 = the 5 key, or pad Y while RB is held; action 91 = Shift, pad X (pad ids decoded from the pad mask builder, see Input_UpdateActionRow). Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? Live: every read of the recipe (level and mode while holding and not holding, in an enemy turn, in a dialogue and on the world map); the EventControl timers during a hold; level 2 with Y + RB or the 5 key. ? What dword_140D3A840 is, and so in which battle moments the level is not refreshed.

name: FormulaHandlerContract
scope: The 106 ability formula handlers and the blocks they call
summary: What a formula handler may assume and has to leave behind, read from the stock handlers and from Battle_ResolveAction: the frame it is called in, how it says 'no effect', which result fields go together, why it must not roll during a preview, the two-sided result, the post-processing it does not control, and the ability ids the shared blocks compare.

behavior.text: frame: a handler is entered through call [r12 + rax * 8] with no argument and its return value ignored (0x140309F53); everything it needs is in globals: the caster unit (g_BattleCasterUnit), the target unit (g_BattleActingUnit), the target's result block (g_BattleActionBlock), the caster's result block (g_BattleCasterResult) and g_FormulaBlock (record copies at 0x1407B0794, the weapon at 0x1407B07A8, the inflict row at 0x1407B07B0, the item id at +0x0A, the inflict row index at +0x0D, the faith bytes at +4 / +5, the weapon bonus at +0x17).
both result blocks were reset by Battle_ResultReset just before (hit flag 1, hit percent 100, the rest 0), so a handler only has to lower the hit flag or fill amounts.
no effect: the stock idiom is hit = 0, reason (5 nullified, 6 failed chance, 7 no effect) and hit percent 0, with the amounts left 0; Formula_ChanceRoll also zeroes the amount.

amounts and kind bits go together: the four amount words are signed; every routing block sets the matching kind bit (0x80, 0x40, 0x20, 0x10; 0x08 for a pending status; 0x01 for a stat, gil or EXP change). sub_14030A11C's caller sets kind bit 0x01 afterwards when the flag word is non-zero.

preview and the AI share the handler: g_BattleSimulating is non-zero during a forecast; Battle_Rand15 then returns 0x4000, Formula_ChanceRoll skips its roll unless the chance is 0, Formula_EvadeByteRoll and Formula_BardDancerGate skip their rolls, and the value 2 is tested by Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication (every listed status dropped on the 24 percent roll) and Formula_StatusChance19 (returns false).

two-sided results: an effect on the caster is written to the caster's block with its hit flag 1, the amount word and the kind bit (Formula_DrainHP, Formula_DrainMP, formulas 39, 40, 60, 66, 91); Formula_87 swaps the unit pointers instead. The resolver applies both blocks (I).

post-processing the handler does not control: sub_14030A11C(1) clamps the four amounts to 999, scales HP and MP damage by the difficulty row (only when g_ShopModeGate is non-zero and the unit flag bits at +0x1EE say so), runs the hook row of formulas 6, 14, 15, 16, 23, 47, 48, 71, 72, 74, 75 and 77 only, and clears the hit flag when the hit percent is 0. A formula id with no hook row gets no Undead rule from it; Formula_DrainHP and Formula_DrainMP call the function with 0 themselves.

ids the shared blocks compare: the stored formula id (g_FormulaBlock +0x18) is tested by ten sites (7, 106, 37, 38, 39, 40, 46, 42, 99 and two membership sets); the post step sub_1403067D0 runs only for stored ids below 7; id 100 clears the item word; id 3 uses inflict row 0.

ability-id keyed blocks: Formula_StatusChance19 (219), Formula_ChanceSum (65), Formula_SapStatPick (143 to 145 and 197 to 199), Action_PickTargetEquipment (18 ids), and formulas 28, 29 and 42 read the ability word at g_FormulaBlock +8.

inflict: the statuses a handler adds come from the six-byte inflict record copy chosen by g_FormulaBlock +0x0D (the weapon record's byte +7, the chemist record's byte +2 or the ability record's byte +0x0B; formula 3 forces row 0); Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication applies it, or the handler writes ActionResult +0x1D..+0x26 itself.

open_questions: ? how the result applier consumes the caster's block in every case (I: it applies both); whether a handler may leave the flag word unset when it writes kind bit 0x01 itself.

name: FormulaHandlersBranchOnTheAbilityId
summary: Battle_ResolveAction reads one formula id per action (a byte), clamps it and calls one registry handler; many handlers then branch on the id of the ability being resolved (the formula block's +8 word).

behavior.text: the formula comes from the action record +8 (command kinds 0, 3, 6, 7 and 4), the weapon record +2 (kinds 8, 10), the chemist record +0 (kind 1) or a constant (99, 100, 1); it is clamped ((u8)(id - 1) > 0x69 -> 1), stored once at g_FormulaBlock +0x18 and dispatched once at 0x140309F53; every hop is one byte. Formula_106 re-dispatches with the weapon's byte, unclamped.

the formula block +8 (0x1407B0778) holds the ability being resolved; the songs (28: 86..92), dances (29: 93..99), talk skills (42: 117..121, 123), equipment picks (37, 38, 46: 18 ids), formulas 26 / 43 (143..145, 197..199) and the shared helpers testing ability 0, 65 and 219 read it. Formula 4 writes it (the weapon's spell).

a 106-row per-formula hook table (PostBattleCalc, Battle_Init) gives 12 formulas an Undead rule; formula ids above 106 skip it, and ten readers of +0x18 test stock formula ids (7, 42, 99, 106, sets of 21 and 45 ids).

open_questions: ? the 357 / 358 inflict tests before the dispatch read the own id.

name: FormulaHandlersChooseTheirEffectByAbilityId
summary: Several shared formula handlers choose their effect by the ability id in the formula block's word +8, and the resolver tests a few single ids, so an ability id none of them lists takes the default branch (usually: no effect).

behavior.text: the sap effect (sub_1403064D8, called by Formula_26_StatSap and Formula_43_RendStats): ids 143, 144, 145 and 197, 198, 199; any other id does nothing.
the equipment steal chain (Action_PickTargetEquipment): ids 110..114, 138..141, 160..163 and 361..365 pick which equipped item is taken; any other id returns -1 with no item.

songs (Formula_28_BardSongs): 86..92; dances (Formula_29_DancerDances): 93..99; Speechcraft (Formula_42_Speechcraft): 117..121 and 123; any other id gets the default branch, which only sets the result flag in the songs and dances.

single-id tests the resolver and others make: 65 (Golem) at 0x140305F52 in sub_140305F4C; 219 at 0x140306C30 in sub_140306C10; in Battle_ResolveAction id 358 keeps the inflict index already in the block instead of the action row's byte +11 (0x140309D67) and id 357 skips the clear of the weapon or item word (0x140309D8B); BattlePreview_BuildAction tests 357 at 0x140282306 on the unit's ability word (+0x1A2).

Battle_ResolveAction copies the 20-byte action row (the row of the id, or row 0 for an id above 0x16F) to 0x1407B0794 before it dispatches the formula; the formula id is row byte +8, clamped to 1 when it is above 0x6A, and the handler is g_FormulaHandlers[formula].
the sap function has the cases 143..145 and 197..199; Speechcraft has no case for 122.

notes: The word is the one at 0x1407B0778 = block + 8.
open_questions: ? every other handler that tests the word (the 14 readers are listed on g_FormulaBlock; only the five above were read in full).

name: FormulaIdsPastTheByte
summary: Every hop of a formula id is one byte and the registry has 106 rows; the clamp `(u8)(id - 1) > 0x69 -> 1` sends any other value to formula 1.

behavior.text: sources are the action record +8, the weapon record +2, the chemist record +0 (the formula block's +8 ability word and +0x0A item word name them); the clamp `(u8)(id - 1) > 0x69 -> 1` at 0x140309DAC; one dispatch at 0x140309F53; Formula_106 re-dispatches the weapon byte unclamped; ten readers of block +0x18 test stock formula ids (none names 255).

open_questions: ? formula ids past 106 skip the per-formula Undead hooks.

name: FormulaIdsWithNoHandlerBody
scope: Formula ids 17, 19, 24, 25 and 70 of the formula registry
summary: Five formula ids have no formula of their own: their registry rows point at an empty function, so an action with one of them keeps the reset result (a hit with no amount and no status) and only the post-processing runs.

behavior.text: registry rows 17, 19, 24, 25 and 70 (formula ids, entry id - 1 of the table at 0x140682BD0) all hold 0x1400103E0, a three-byte function that returns at once (the compiler's empty indirect-call check).
the result block was reset by Battle_ResultReset before the handler (hit flag 1, hit percent 100, every amount 0), so such an action lands and changes nothing through the formula.
no stock action, weapon or chemist row names one of these five ids.
formulas 30, 94 and 95 share one handler too (0x140307C10); every other id from 1 to 106 has a handler of its own.

notes: Read 2026-11-18 from the registry rows and the function at 0x1400103E0.

name: FormulaPostHooksAreKeyedByFormulaId
summary: After a formula handler runs, sub_14030A11C looks the formula byte up in a 106-row hook table (PostBattleCalc) and runs the row's callback, if any: twelve formulas have an Undead rule there. The table is indexed by the formula id, so a formula id past 106 has no row.

behavior.text: Battle_Init allocates the object (0xD48 bytes, 106 rows), sub_1401F92A8 fills it, sub_14030A11C reads row (formula - 1) when (formula - 1) < 0x6A (0x14030A2A0) and calls the row's entry when its argument is non-zero.
the formulas that have a callback are 6, 14, 15, 16, 23, 47, 48, 71, 72, 74, 75 and 77; every other row is the empty marker.

notes: Source: IDA reads of 2026-11-12.
open_questions: ? the effect of the last five callbacks in full.

name: GenericUnitSpriteNumberFromJob
summary: A generic unit has no stored sprite number: the game derives it from the job and the sex, with the same sum in at least ten places, and every other job id falls back to a default.

behavior.basis: (address list checked to exist in our database)
behavior.text: the sprite number of a male generic unit is twice the job id minus 0x34 and a female unit's is one more (Mime, 0x5D, one lower); the sum is computed at 0x1402C082F (Unit_GetSpriteSetId), 0x1402B573F (PartyUnit_BuildJobRecord), 0x1402DB44D, 0x1403009BD, 0x140300F95 and 0x14032ABEA, each reading the job byte twice, and Unit_ResolvePreviewShape computes (job + 0x26) * 2 + the sprite set.
Job_IdToIndex returns job - 74 for jobs 74 to 93, job - 140 for 160 and 161, and 0 for every other id, so an unknown job id selects the first job's slot (the Squire's), not an error.

the sprite byte of a battle actor sits at actor +0xA and is copied from the per-unit graphics record array (sprite id at +1 of each 0x32D6-byte record); a roster record's first byte is the sprite set: below 0x80 a story sprite number, 0x80 a male generic unit, 0x81 a female one, 0x82 a monster.

for a sprite pair (S, S + 1), S even, the job value (S + 0x34) / 2 makes the game's own sum give S for men and S + 1 for women; the values for the spare pairs 88/89, 90/91, 92/93, 94/95, 156/157 and 164 to 169 are 70 to 73, 104 and 108 to 110, none of which the functions special-case.

open_questions: ? the six sprite readers in the battle code (0x2DB09C, 0x300768, 0x300D74, 0x32AB3C) were not each decompiled by us.

name: GuideBarLayout
summary: The guide bar shows one UIButtonGuide key at a time: up to 8 slots, left ones first then right ones from x 1920; a sub-row mask hides sub-rows.

behavior.text: UIGuide_Set jumps to the guide agent (agents array entry 14, +112) when it is active (its vtable +16); its add-on +64 gets GuideBar_SetPage(addon, key, rows), which stores the key at +2224 and a sub-row mask at +2228 and lays the bar out.

GuideBar_Layout reads UI table 33 (`UIButtonGuide`): rows of the key, left ones, then right ones; GuideBar_LayoutRow skips sub-row i when bit i of the mask is clear and a row whose text id (+12) is 0; byte +37 (`Unknown25`) = right side.

UIGuide_Show(_, show, 0, rows) calls the guide agent's 0x14013C740; the settings screen hides the bar when it opens its own confirm and shows it again when the confirm closes; TitleMenu_Build ends with show 0.

name: GUITextNodeStringSource
scope: where a text node's string comes from: the UI table or the code
summary: A text node shows the string of its UI table text id while that id is not 0; with text id 0 it keeps a string set in code.

behavior.text: `GUITextNode_SetString` (0x1403F0F8C) copies the string into the node.
`GUITextNode_UpdateLayout` re-reads the text from the UI table only while the node's text id (+248) is not 0, so a text node with text id 0 keeps a string set in code.

name: HdSheetAndClassicPaletteLoading
summary: How a sprite number becomes a sheet and a palette: a g2d entry pair through the HD table and the pack's unchecked index table, and a palette from the classic file named in the classic table.

behavior.text: CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture reads the entry from the HD table (no sheet above 0xA9; -1 for sprites 155 to 158 means entry 160 with a palette from file kind 72), then loads entry and entry + 1 through sub_1403D2450, PackFile_ReadEntry and sub_1403D25A4 from the pack handle qword_140D3AD58.
sub_1403D2450 and PackFile_EntryPtr index the pack's 16-byte offset rows with the entry number and no bound check.

the palette comes from CharaPalette_LoadClassic (first 0x200 bytes of the classic file, then the CharShape colour override); the sheet's pixels are 4-bit indexes into it, so the colours follow the classic file.
CharaPalette_LoadClassic has no bound on the sprite number; it reads the pair at table + 8 * sprite.

name: HdSheetFromSlotColoursFromRecord
summary: In Enhanced a pool's HD sheet comes from its sheet slot (the g2d entry) while its colours come from the pool record's palette.

behavior.text: seen live 2026-11-13: a goblin record holding another unit's palette drew the goblin sheet in that unit's colours (the sheet slot held the goblin's entry 1070).

g_HdSheetEntryBySlot (0x142E7FE6C, 30 dwords) holds the g2d entry of each HD sheet slot, -1 = not set; look pool p (0..9) uses slot 20 + p: SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry (0x14026F047 / 0x14026F020) writes hd_entry_by_shape[sprite] there when the sprite is in range and its entry is not -1; sub_140260CF0 fills a slot that is -1 from the scene unit's sprite byte at its next draw.

HdLayer_BindSheetTexture binds the HD texture ids of pool sheets (123 + 16 p + frame) to dword_142E7FEBC[p] (= slot 20 + p); HdLayer_BuildTextures loads an entry that differs from the slot's loaded one with PackFile_ReadEntry.

PackFile_ReadEntry (0x1403D25D8) = PackEntry_Inflate(state, out, PackFile_EntryPtr(pack, n), size) with no test of n against the pack's entry count; the first access to the entry tests its flag byte +4 (0x1403D1EF0). An entry number past the pack faults there (seen live 2026-11-13).

name: HitLabelsAndThePanelEffectLineAreSeparateLists
summary: The status label over a unit hit by an action and the effect line of the unit status panel are two different lists. The hit label maps a status to its BattleSignal row through the fixed 40-byte tbl_StatusBattleSignal; the panel maps it through UIStatusEffect (field +20 non-zero, field +24 the BattleSignal row). Both start from the result block's 40-bit added and removed sets.

behavior.text: StatusList_BuildFromResultBlock and UnitPanel_SetSignalList ran while the action preview was up and on enemy turns, and not when the action's result showed over the hit unit.
the hit labels never read UIStatusEffect to choose the row; only the icon is looked up there, by the BattleSignal key.
a status outside the 40-bit sets showed no label over the hit unit; with its BattleSignal id appended to the task queue after the game's walk, it showed its title and its own icon.
the action preview resolves the action with the forecast mode 2 (the dword at 0x14186AF80); the result shown over the hit unit comes from the action's real pass (mode 0).
after the pass on the target, Battle_ResolveAction ran again with the acting unit as its target; the target then countered (Counter shown), so the second pass is taken to be the reaction check.

name: ItemCommandRelation
scope: how the Item command and Throw turn an item id into an ability id and back
summary: An Item-command use is an item id plus a paired ability id: the table maps abilities 368..381 to items 240..253, while at use the engine computes ability = item + 0x80 and the current-action builder computes item = ability - 0x80. Throw is a second table of equipment categories, and a consumable's effect is a chemist row, not the item record.

behavior.text: the table has 14 rows: ability 368 + i is item 240 + i. The list builder accepts only 368..381 and writes a byte item list terminated by 0xFF.

at use the relation runs as arithmetic in the other direction: the unit action word stores ability = item + 0x80, and the current-action builder subtracts 0x80 to recover the item id before it reads the chemist row.
the builder also reads the table directly through an address derived as its base minus 0x170, with no range check, so a value outside the 14 rows reads what follows the table.
an item enters the Item command only when its record's equipment category byte is 0x22 (34); action resolution independently requires Item_IsInCategory(item, 6). The two gates read different data.

Throw selects a row of the 12-byte category table with the item's equipment category. The item must also be a weapon-slot item with weapon flags bit 1 set, and the list builder only scans ids below 256.
a consumable's effect is its 3-byte chemist row (formula id, amount, inflicted status); the animation and effect number come from the paired ability id, not from the item id.
items 254 and 255 have chemist rows but no row in the 14-row table, so the Item menu cannot offer them; the use path would still build abilities 382 and 383, which are Throw abilities.
the undo path refuses every id of 261 and above, so a consumable above 260 cannot be refunded by the stock code even though the use path can consume it.

because item + 0x80 is stored without a mask but the AI and preview path reads only ten id bits, an item id above 895 loses its high bits on that path; the request and the unit action block keep the full 16-bit id.
a consumable therefore needs three rows at once: an item record with category 0x22, a chemist row, and a paired ability in the table's range with animation and effect rows.

notes: V: the gates, the arithmetic and the table readers are named in the sheets of the functions involved.
open_questions: ? which consumer turns the six throwing-weapon item ids 122..127 into a throw ability; the AI branch adds those ids in the 10-bit field, but the later step was not traced.

name: ItemDisplayInShopAndEquipPanels
scope: the shop lists and the equipment detail panel for an item id
summary: What a shop row and the detail panel show for an item, all keyed by the item id: name and description from the Item-en row, price from the item record, icon files named by the id.

behavior.text: the name is ItemTable_GetName(id) and the description ItemTable_GetRow(id) +16: nxd Item-en (table 45) by key.
the price is ShopEntry +24, from the exe item record.

the icons are the files ui/ffto/icon/equip_item_s/textureparts/ei_s_<id>_uitx (list, Icon row 13) and ui/ffto/icon/equip_item/textureparts/ei_<id>_uitx (detail panel, Icon row 12); retail ships ids 0..260.

with the contiguous-keys flag kept on a table whose keys have a gap (Item-en keys 0..260 plus 300), the table had first key 0, last key 300 and 262 rows, so key 300 asked row position 300 and found nothing; the text setters then leave their nodes (I: the Rod's texts the owner saw were left from the previous item).
no remap (IdRemap_Lookup) is on these paths; the list holds the id itself.

notes: The icon needs the two files named by the id.

name: ItemIdSpace
scope: the item functions and every bound on an item id
summary: Item ids are u16 wherever they are stored for units (roster, party, battle and preview records), but the code bounds them in three ways: the item functions serve 0..0x104 (two stock record arrays split at 0x100), about 39 code sites compare an id with 0x105 (or 0x104 / 0x103) before using it, and several stores have exactly 261 entries (inventory, Poachers' Den, new flags, item order lists). Menu and battle paths mask ids with 0x1FF or 0x3FF.

behavior.text: ItemIcon_Set (item icons) takes ids below 0x200; the hand-slot readers of the unit panels mask with 0x1FF, the menus with 0x3FF; bit 14 (0x4000) of a menu list entry marks an item the unit cannot equip.
the menus list only items present in the saved item order lists (ItemOrder_FilterList drops the others); those lists are filled for ids 1..260 by ItemOrder_SyncGroup and have fixed capacities.
five display functions derive the 255 empty-slot sentinel from the 0x105 bound register (bound minus 6).

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.

name: ItemMenuListWordMarkOverlapsLargeIds
summary: A shop or equip list word holds the item id in its low bits and the 'cannot equip' mark in bit 14; an item id can be up to 15 bits wide, so for an id of 16,384 and above the id's own bit 14 and the mark are the same bit.

behavior.text: a list word is the item id, with 0x4000 ORed in when the unit cannot equip the item and the list is built in mode 1; the list ends at 0xFFFF.
the game's own equip functions refuse a word with bits above 14 set, so an item id is at most 0x7FFF and bit 15 of a list word is never set by an id; bit 14 is the id's own for ids from 16,384.

an id of 16,384 or more and an id below 16,384 with the mark are the same word, so a reader cannot tell them apart from the word alone; every stock reader that masks the word to an id first (steps 5 to 7 of ItemMenuListLifecycle) uses the stock mask 0x3FF or a wider one and then tests bit 14 of the original or of the loaded value.

behavior.basis: (seen live, item ids above the stock range placed in the item table)
behavior.text: ids up to 16,383 listed in the Outfitter Buy and Sell lists; ids 16,384, 20,000 and 32,000 did not appear in either, the cut being exactly at 0x4000.

ItemOrder_FilterList runs on g_MenuList right after the mode-1 builds and rewrites it in the saved order, so any per-row side data indexed by list position ends up on another row as soon as the saved order is not the id order; the mark of a row belongs to its id, not to its slot.

notes: The party hand word has its own layout (PartyHandWord): there bit 15 is the picked-or-bought-in-this-visit flag, never set on a list word.
open_questions: ? whether the mark was ever meant to be read by the Classic item pages for ids above 0x3FF.

name: JobArrayAccessesPutTheRecordPointerInTheIndexRegister
summary: Nine accesses of the per-unit job arrays are written with the byte offset in the register that stands first in the address and the pointer into the record in the register that stands second, so the record pointer is not the first register of the address.

behavior.text: the level read of JobRecord_FromJobId (0x1400FBE09) is a one-byte load whose first register holds the job index halved (Job_IdToIndex, shift right by one at 0x1400FBE06) and whose second register holds the key's pointer to the level array; the even or odd index then selects the high or low nibble.

the learned-bit reads and writes have the same shape: Job_ReadLearnedBitsForBattle (0x14020D1E5 word read, 0x14020D22F byte OR), Job_LearnAbilityByMenu (0x14028942B, 0x140289435, and two accesses at displacement 0xBD from 0x1402894BF), sub_14030CD08 (0x14030CDDE), sub_1403170CC (0x140317144) and Unit_TryLearnAbility (0x140278192): the offset is 3 times the job index plus the array start in one register, the record pointer in the other.
the count of nine comes from the stage reading; the disassembly scan of the six functions lists these instructions with two registers in the address and no scale.

none of the nine tests the job index against a limit: the address is array start plus the offset, so an index larger than the array's own length reads and writes whatever follows the array, in the same record or in the next one.

notes: The sizes of the arrays are in JobArraysInThePartyRecordHoldStockIndicesOnly.

name: JobArraysInThePartyRecordHoldStockIndicesOnly
summary: In the 640-byte party record the per-job arrays are sized for the stock job indices, so an access with a larger index leaves its own array and, from a certain index, the record.

behavior.text: record B (640 bytes, 55 of them): unlock mask +120 (3 bytes), learned bits +123 (66 bytes, 3 per job index) ending in a word at +187, job levels +189 (12 bytes, one nibble per index), current job points +202 (46 bytes, one word per index), second points array +248 (46 bytes) (PartyUnit_FillFromWork copies them from the save record).

the level of index n sits at +189 + n/2, so from n = 902 the address is outside the record (189 + 451 = 640) and in the record that follows; the learned bits of index n sit at +123 + 3n, so from n = 173 they start past the 640 bytes (123 + 3 x 172 = 639 is the last that starts inside), and below that, from n = 22, they overlap the level, points and later arrays of the same record.

Job_IdToIndex answers 0 for every job id outside 74..93 and 160..161 (see UnlockMaskStreamRunsIntoLearnedBitsPastIndex23), so a stock job never produces a large index; an index above 23 reaches these arrays only from data that names such a job.
the next record after a party record is the next party unit, so a read through an index past the record returns another unit's level or learned bits (zero for a unit with none).

notes: Record letters and offsets as in PartyUnit_FillFromWork and the sheets that cite A, B and C.
open_questions: ? the exact learned-bit overlap for indices 24 to 172 (they land on fields the stock code never reads at those offsets).

name: JobCardComesFromTheJobTypeRow
scope: engine (job card art on the Status screen)
summary: The job card (the large faded painting behind the right half of the Status panel) is chosen by the job's JobType row, not by the job row's TexturePartsIndex (that is the small job icon): Job row +24 names a JobType row, whose MaleVisualIconId / FemaleVisualIconId name an Icon row holding the card's part file path.

behavior.text: JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag reads the job row, then the JobType row (UI table 0xC8) by the job row's +24, and stores the icon id at out[0]: the female id for a record whose +8 byte is 0 or above, the male id otherwise.
Icon rows 701..738 hold 'job_visual/textureparts/jv_NN_<m|f>_uitx.utexpt'; Icon rows 739.. are blank, JobType rows 115..124 are blank (0 / 0).

a card part file is 93 bytes: a 0x20-byte header (u16 652 at +0x18 and 400 at +0x1C: the picture's height and width), the texture path, then 'TexturePart'; the u32 at +0x0C is the offset of 'TexturePart' counted from +0x0C. The texture is 400 x 652 RGBA: the figure's silhouette at about 70 % opacity (alpha at most 182), fading toward the lower left (about 215 + x / 2 - 0.54 y), clear outside the figure (measured over the 38 stock cards).
Ramza shows no card in any job; a generic unit shows its job's card (the female Knight's for a female Knight).
a job row naming another JobType showed that type's card; one naming a JobType whose Icon row has a new part file showed the new picture.

notes: The JobType id also feeds the per-type flag array and Job_SameJobType (see the field notes in data/jobs/fields.jsonl).

name: JobChangeReachesTheSaveRecordOnlyThroughWriteBack
scope: engine (Jobs screen, party and save records)
summary: Changing a unit's job on the Jobs screen changes the save record's job byte (+2) in exactly one place: PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave copies the low byte of the party record's job word (+0x24) into it.

behavior.basis: (write watch on save record 0 +2, 80 s, Ramza changed from Ninja to Knight with Change Job on the Jobs screen, 2026-11-04)
behavior.text: the byte went 0x59 to 0x4C, and all 4 accesses came from PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave (the store at 0x1402857DB; the instruction after it reports). No other function wrote the byte during the change.

the save record is g_UnitSaveData + 0x258 * (signed word at party +0x2C); the stored byte is the low byte of the party word at +0x24 (a byte load from party +0x24, a byte store to save +2), and PartyUnit_FillFromWork stores that word as a 16-bit value (0x140284AF1), so the party record can hold an id wider than the save byte.
the other stores of the byte (work-to-save, spawn, event unit setup) were not exercised by this change.

name: JobChangeTransitionShapeFromTheListEntryByte
summary: While a job change plays its light pillar, the Status header figure is drawn in a shape JobScreen_UpdateState asks Unit_ResolvePreviewShape for, passing the Change Job list entry's job as one byte; for a generic unit that shape is the character byte + 2 x (job + 38), one byte.

behavior.text: at 0x140368F9A JobScreen_UpdateState loads r8b from g_RuntimeJobList (2 bytes an entry) at the list cursor and calls Unit_ResolvePreviewShape (unit, outPalette, job); the result's low byte is stored as the shape.

Unit_ResolvePreviewShape reads jobs 92 and 93 one lower; for character byte 0x80 / 0x81 it answers the character + 31 for job 160, + 33 for 161 and 164, else the character + 2 x (job + 38); a named character (below 0x80) gets its own byte; 0x82, 0xA2..0xA9 and 0xA5 have rows of their own.

a list entry whose job id is 300 was drawn during the pillar as the figure of job 44 (300's low byte): a grey-haired figure in purple and gold; after the pillar the Status figure is drawn by its own path.

name: JobLearnedBitsPointerIsBuiltFromTheUnitRecord
summary: The readers of a job's learned bits compute a pointer into the unit record (unit record + 123 + 3 * job index) and hand it to the bit reader, which reads 24 bits = 3 bytes.

behavior.text: sub_14028ACD8, JobAbilityList_Build, sub_14028A474 and sub_140392620 each compute rec + 3 * (index + 41) (or + 0x36 * 3) and hand it to the bit reader (qword_143C49BF0 / qword_143C5C938), which reads 24 bits = 3 bytes.

name: JobLevelZeroDrawsDashesAndGreysChangeJob
scope: engine (Change Job grid and job popup)
summary: A job whose level reads as 0 draws 'Lv. --' on the Change Job grid cell, shows level, EXP and JP as '--' in the job popup, and cannot be chosen: its Change Job entry is greyed.

name: JobListEntryWordMeaning
summary: How JobList_Build fills an entry and what the readers do with its three parts: the id is the low 13 bits the mask keeps, bit 13 means locked for the whole party, and bit 14 means the unit's own job in mode 2 and 'unlocked by another party member' in mode 3.

JobTree_FillJobRecords turns the word into the record state: bit 13 gives state 2, else bit 14 gives state 1, else state 0; a unit whose job is hidden from the tree gets a list of length 1.

name: JobTreeLayerList
scope: the layer slots of a UI frame and, for the Job Tree screen, which component opens each one and how its float rectangle is made
summary: A UI layer is not tied to a component by any pointer: the layer records hold no component link (only the mask component of a masked layer is stored). The list of layers of a frame is a pure function of the draw traversal: widgets are drawn from the last vector entry to the first, inside a widget the component trees are walked last child first, a component with an enabled effect group (or the widget root) opens a layer slot, the parent continues in a new slot after every child layer, and a slot without any draw is reused. The float rectangle of a layer is the union of the integer bounds of the quads drawn into it, grown by the blur reach of its effects and by 16 pixels and clamped to the target. The Job Tree frame read live had 27 slots (26 used) for the screen's four drawing widgets.

behavior.text: rectangle rule, step 1 (draws). UIRender_AccumulateQuadBounds raises the double bounds r+152..+176 with the four transformed corners of every emitted quad (min x, min y, max x, max y, layout pixels of the target). GUILayer_Flush (run at every layer switch and at the end of the frame) turns them into integers with GUILayer_BoundsToRect (left = trunc(min x), top = trunc(min y), right = trunc(max x + 1), bottom = trunc(max y + 1), truncation toward zero) and, when the result is non-empty, merges it into the slot's dirty rectangle r + 512 * slot + 41824 (replace when that is empty, else union). The dirty rectangles and the layer ids are cleared every frame by GUIRenderer_ResetFrame. So the dirty rectangle of a layer is the union over all of its quads of [trunc(min), trunc(max + 1)) in x and y.

rectangle rule, step 2 (GUILayer_ExpandBounds, once per slot after the last widget). If the dirty rectangle is empty the layer rectangle is not written. Otherwise radius R = max(0, float layer+500 when the kind dword layer+28 is 1, layer+188 when the shadow byte +177 is set, layer+204 when the glow byte +178 is set, layer+180 when the single-float byte +176 is set); pad P = 0 for R <= 0, else f * UIBlur_TapCount(R / f, 1/255) with f = 1 (R <= 3.2), 2 (<= 6.4), 4 (<= 12.8), 8 (<= 25.6), 16 (<= 51.2), 32; examples: R 0.667 gives 3, 0.8 gives 3, 1.0 gives 4, 2.0 gives 6, 2.667 gives 8, 4.0 gives 12, 6.0 gives 16, 6.667 gives 20; every edge grows by P, then by 16, then is clamped to [0, 1280] x [0, 720] (W, H = r+184 / r+188); the layer rectangle (x, y, w, h) = (x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0) as floats at layer+208..+220. A layer entirely off the target ends with w or h = 0. An effect group whose flag byte is clear adds nothing, whatever stale radius the record still holds.

the integer rectangle that GUILayer_PackAtlasRect derives (layer+240..+252) is therefore (x0', y0', x1', y1') with the clamped edges above; the live check on 26 + 40 used layers matched exactly (a drop-shadow layer of radius 2.0 gets P = 6, a glow of 2.667 gets 8, a single-float group of 0.667 gets 3).

a software renderer needs no component link for the rectangle: it knows the quads of each layer, takes the union of their [trunc(min), trunc(max + 1)) bounds, and applies the pad of the layer's strongest effect radius, the 16 pixel margin and the clamp. The radii are the UIB radius times the layer scale min(sx, sy) (GUILayer_BuildRecord; 2/3 at 720p).

component <-> layer link. The 592-byte layer record (r + 303480 + 592 * slot) and the 512-byte slot block (r + 512 * slot + 41336: 488 bytes of context copy, dirty rectangle, layer id, flag) contain no pointer to a component, widget or node, with one exception: the context copy of a masked layer (the layer of a component whose mask is a component) holds the mask component at ctx+392 and its Mask node at ctx+400 (live scan of all 27 slots for any component or widget address). The only other per-component value that survives is the layer id (ctx+548 = u16 comp+552 << 16, 0 for every component of the Job Tree). The link is therefore the traversal itself: replay GUICore_CommitFrame over the object tree (widget vector at core+24, components at widget+104, component node tree at comp+272, reference nodes kind 12 with the cached component at node+304 and the name keys at node+208 / +224) and count slots as below.

slot machine (r = the UI renderer, count r+606584, current r+606588, draw counter r+606592). A draw (an image, text, rect, nine-grid, digit node, ...) increments the draw counter and records quads into the current slot. GUILayer_SetCurrent(-1) flushes (the counter merges into the slot, and the count grows when the current slot is the last one) and selects the slot index = count. ComponentLayer_Begin opens a layer when the component's effect collector returns 1 or the force rule applies (widget root: always, since widget byte +83 is 1; other components: byte comp+561): GUILayer_Select builds a record from the component context in the slot at index count (an existing record is reused only for a non-zero layer id with compatible settings). After a child component that opened a layer GUIComponentRef_Draw calls GUILayer_Select with the PARENT context: a new record at the next index with the parent's (inherited) effect groups, and every later draw of any component goes into it until another layer opens. A layer that received no draw leaves the count alone, so its slot is rebuilt by the next layer. At the end of a widget the open record is flushed and reset.

a component with a mask component (comp+244 group resolving to a component, ctx+409): before its own layer is built ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent draws the mask component into the next slot (default record, flag +487 = 1, no layers inside it), and the component's layer follows in the slot after it (flags +489 = 1). A component with an image mask (ctx+384) opens only its own layer.

the widget loop. GUICore_CommitFrame walks the widget vector from the last entry to the first (descending priority word w+62 along the vector, so ascending priority in draw order) and draws the widgets whose byte +74 or +75 is non-zero and +79 is zero. The two bar draws after the loop (GUICore_DrawOutsideBars for the layer transform whose int at +128 is 1) add a draw counter without quads, so the last slot of the frame is a counted empty slot (live: slot 26, dirty (0, 0, 0, 0), not used).

inside a component, GUINode_DrawChildren starts at the first child, follows the +32 links to the last sibling and draws backwards through +40, so the last list entry is drawn first (bottom) and the first entry last (top); kinds: 1 container (recurse; Layer / LayerRoot nodes open nothing), 2 image, 3 text, 4 nine-grid, 5, 6 rect, 7, 8, 10, 12 component reference, 14 virtual; kinds 9 (Mask), 11 and 13 (Collision) draw nothing. A reference is skipped when its node is hidden (+204 = 0 or +145 set), when the component is missing, disabled (+416 = 0) or has the opacity group with +188 <= 0.

components of the Job Tree widget (752 in memory) that can open a layer: UnitSelect (glow group, 23 of them), the Route* arrows (30, glow group) and Line* pieces (11, glow group) when their glow strength or radius is above 0, Cross (5, single-float group when its value is above 0), TextBoardJobName (23, drop-shadow group, always on while visible), TextMask of the main tab (drop shadow plus a component mask: TextBoard01 of ffto_main_tab) and the two BGBlur instances (opacity / blur group, comp+192: kind 1 layers, hidden in the frame read). Components with no effect group never open a layer and draw into the enclosing slot: Widget (the root, which does open one), JobTree, Unit, UnitJob, UnitBase, BG, BGStone, TextBoardUse, TextBoardJobLv, MainTab, Tab, TextBoard01..04, Black, BlackNoBlur.

name: JobTreePanelCountLimits
summary: What bounds the number of Job Tree panels: the immediate widths of the count and cap compares, the render slots 80 + panel and the per-panel arrow capacity.

behavior.text: the tree addon has 6 count sites (the panel count, 20) and 13 cap sites (19); 4 of the 6 count sites (0x140133941, 0x140133D6F, 0x1401340DF, 0x140368B15) and all 13 cap sites are compares with an 8-bit immediate (the other two count sites load a 32-bit immediate), and an imm8 is sign-extended, so those compares hold values up to 127 only.
all 17 one-byte sites are compares with a sign-extended 8-bit immediate; an immediate of 0x80..0xFF compares as -128..-1 (the signed loops end after one pass, the unsigned caps bound nothing).

panel storage is linear: panel nodes at +72 with stride 456, panel records (148 bytes) after them, then a 96-byte tail; the object is allocated by an operator new whose size immediate is one of those sites.

JobTree_SetPanelRecord gives panel p the render slot 80 + p (store of v4 + 80 into the record at +92) and CharaRender_SetSlotRequest refuses slot numbers above 255, so panels 0..175 can hold a sprite; the job-change cells use 61 + cell.
the final loop of JobTree_FillJobRecords draws 6 arrows per panel (6 requirement slots) over a panel count compare against the immediate 0x14; JobTree_RefreshAddon gives each panel 4 label boards.
a panel's content is chosen by list position, not by job id: JobTree_SetPanelRecord stores a record in panel `pos` (+1 for jobs 92 and 93).
every panel needs its own node set in the layout file ffto_job_tree.uib under a stem name (JobTree_NodeStem answers a fixed table for 0..19 and the empty string above).
the number of nodes or the file size the layout loader accepts was not measured.

name: JobTreePanelLookups
scope: the per-panel lookups, the pad step and the scrolling root of the Job Tree
summary: The tree is built for panel numbers 0..19. Four per-panel lookups drive it: the node stem (JobTree_NodeStem), the GeneralJob row (requirement and pad-navigation neighbours), the record slot (JobTree_SetPanelRecord) and the click target (JobList_SelectEntry). The pad step moves the focus by the GeneralJob neighbour rows; the whole tree is one root node.

behavior.text: the stem of panel p comes from JobTree_NodeStem at four call sites of JobTree_RefreshAddon (the panel loop and the three arrow-name builds); it answers the empty string for p >= 20, and the function writes only rax and edx while its callers keep rcx / ecx across it (the level of an arrow name is read back from ecx after the call).

the requirement of panel p is the GeneralJob row with KEY p (one UITable_GetRowByKey(0xBD, p) call in JobTree_RefreshAddon). The same row supplies the 14 pad-navigation neighbours (unknown30..64), where 20 means none.
JobTree_SetPanelRecord(tree, rec, pos) stores the record in panel pos (+1 for jobs 92 / 93) when pos is within the addon's panel count; the fill loop passes the LIST POSITION.
a click on panel p sends the list entry p - 1 (p >= 18) as screen message 128 to JobList_SelectEntry.

the position code of a requirement row is the EXIT side of the arrow from the required panel (1 left, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 top; V against the 19 stock rows, where code 3 pairs with an arrow entering the target from above).
the 21-entry table of 512-byte entries in JobTree_FillJobRecords (loop bound 21) is g_PreviewUnitTable, indexed by a party unit's save index, not by panel.
a required panel has room for 6 dependents (record +0x118): a seventh dependent on one required job gets its arrow drawn but no lit state.

behavior.basis: (executable bytes at the 17 one-byte count and cap sites of the tree, 2026-11-08)
behavior.text: every one is a compare with a sign-extended 8-bit immediate, so the tree holds at most 127 panels; a byte of 0x80 and above would compare as a negative number (the signed panel loops would stop after one pass, the unsigned caps would bound nothing).
a requirement id in a GeneralJob row read by the tree is a tree index (the requirement source and requirement.jobIndex compares are capped at the panel count - 1).

the floor behind the panels is the BG reference of the JobTree component (base fill Rect03 2100 x 1100, the tiled stone image BGStone/Image01, the edge fades Rect00 / Rect01, all with pivot mode 0); it is part of the tree root, so it scrolls with the panels.

the pad direction is read by JobTree_HandleInput as the four bytes at qword_143CD9EE8 + 13648 (down, left, up, right), else the four at + 13652 in the same order; up wins over down, right over left; the game numbers the eight directions clockwise from RIGHT (live 2026-11-08: pad right reads 0, down 2, left 4, up 6), -1 none.

the game's own tests run before the step, in this order: Input_TestAction(0, 0, 26) or the held flag (confirm), then Input_TestAction(0, 0, 27) (cancel). With selector 0 Input_TestAction only reads a table, so asking it twice in a frame changes nothing.

the stock step starts at the panel under the cursor (addon field 12232) when it is a panel, else at the remembered panel (12236) when it is below the panel count, and skips the Bard / Dancer panel the gender flag hides.
the target is focused with GUICore_FocusNode(addon + 72 + 456 x panel); the focus arrives as event 19 and lights the panel's arrows through JobTree_OnCursorEnter.
the ffto_job_tree.uib widget is one root node (1920 x 1080, no parent, at (0, 0)); GUINode_SetPosition on it moved the whole tree and back exactly; the footer (another widget) stayed.

the root is found from a panel node by following the parent pointer (+0x18) to the node with no parent; a panel's place in root coordinates is the sum of the local positions (+56 / +60) below the root.
JobTree_OnFocusChange with focus 1409 (the tree gains the input focus: the screen opens, or the player comes back from the job list) refocuses the remembered panel.
