name: JobTreeViewControl
scope: what a smooth stick scroll and a zoom of the Job Tree can use
summary: The tree root is one node; its position (scroll) and scale are plain integer / float fields whose change reaches every panel, arrow, label and the finger cursor's target in the same UI pass. The game has a stick-scroll pattern for lists that keeps the cursor where it is until it leaves the view. Nothing in the tree reads a stick.

behavior.text: scale is stored at node +80 / +84 (GUINode_SetScale) and enters the node's local matrix about the pivot; a child's matrix is its local matrix times the parent's, and the accumulated scale is kept at +184 / +188 (GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix). A scale on the root therefore scales every descendant that is drawn through these matrices; the root's pivot is (960, 540), so a zoom is about the screen centre.

the finger cursor's target is GUIWidget_GetNodeScreenRect of the focused panel node: its corners go through the node's matrix and every ancestor's. A moved or scaled root is followed by the glove with no extra code (the glove glides toward the new target, 40 percent of the gap per UI frame), but the rect is rounded to integers.

mouse hit tests (GUIWidget_HitTestPoint -> HitTestChildren, GUINode_ComputeRectInMatrix) rectangle-test each node through the accumulated matrix, so a scaled root should hit-test scaled; not seen live.
the tree widget's own stock scroll is absent.

the game's pattern for stick scrolling with a focused item is ListScroll_HandleStick / ListScroll_Step: the right stick scrolls the list whole rows at a time and the focus is only moved (to the first or last visible item) when the focused item has left the view; the free pointer of FreeCursor_StepFromSticks moves axis x frame time x 10 px.
the unused controls on this screen are both sticks, both triggers and the stick clicks (no reader); LB / RB are the unit switch of the job list but not read by the tree.
the footer is another widget and stays when the tree root moves; the 'Job Tree' title and the floor are part of the root and scroll with it.

the tree's moved and scaled node is the widget's root node ('Widget', kind 1); its child 'JobTree' is a reference node (kind 12, position 0, scale 1) whose component object is at node +304; that component's own node (+0x110) has the children LayerRoot (panels and arrows, at (0, 32)), MainTab (title band), BG (the floor plate, at (185, 0), pivot = its size / 2) and BGBlur (hidden). A node's name key at +16 resolves through the interned name table at 0x143CDA2A0 (bucket = low 16 bits, 1-based, 32 bytes each, entry vector at +16 / +24 of 16-byte entries, the first word the name); children chain from +208 through the sibling at +32.

clipping: nothing found that clips the tree widget to a rectangle other than the screen; a component has an optional clip-rectangle effect group (comp +216, ComponentEffects_Collect) that the tree does not enable (not checked per component).

open_questions: ? live: set the root scale to 0.75 through gamecall (GUINode_SetScale on the root) and look at the picture, the glove and a mouse hover; ? the footer and title bands that a clamp should keep clear.

name: KoLeavesSomeStatusesOnTheUnit
summary: KO does not end every status: its property row (status 2) cancels the action states 4..7, Confusion, Vampire, Float, Invisibility, Berserk, Critical and every status 23..39, and leaves Undead, Stone, Traitor, Blindness, Silence, Oil, Reraise, Chicken and Toad on a KO'd unit. Reraise acts on the KO'd unit at its next turn.

behavior.text: a Squire with Reraise was KO'd by an attack (+0x61 held KO 0x20 of byte 0 and Reraise 0x20 of byte 2, the applied set only KO); at her next turn she revived with 4 HP (41 / 10) and the Reraise was used up (no longer applied, Reraise bit clear).
g_StatusPropertyTable row 2 bytes +6..+10 (data/tables/exe_status.jsonl id 2: cancels 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 20, 23..39).
Battle_StatusApply copies the applied status's cancels into the pending remove before it sets the bit, so applying KO removes those statuses.
BTurn_OnTurnStartStatus revives a unit that is KO, not Undead and has Reraise: heal max HP / 10 (at least 1), KO and Reraise into the pending remove.

name: LayerAtlasPlacement
scope: every layer of a UI frame that is packed (composited, kind 0 or 1, none of the flags +78 / +486 / +488); the Job Tree frame was checked end to end
summary: Where a UI layer's pixels are placed in the layer atlas each frame: the layers are put in a fixed order (their order key), and a shelf packer places each layer's integer rectangle plus a margin of 2 px (32 px when a blur above 3.2 is present) row by row into pages of the target size; the placed content rectangle P replaces the layer rectangle and P minus the integer screen origin is the atlas offset. The recipe below reproduced x, y and page of all 63 layers of a running Job Tree frame.

behavior.text: inputs. The target size (W, H) = the u16 values at +20 / +22 of UILayer_GetTarget(layer): the layer's own target or the renderer's current one (1280 x 720 for every layer of the live frame; all layers shared one target). Per used layer (byte +76), in slot order (slot = the record index = the order the frame created them in; layer+12 starts as the slot index every frame): the float rectangle (x, y, w, h) at +208..+220, the kind dword +28, the flag bytes +78, +79, +177, +178, +179, +486, +487, +488, +489, and the floats +180, +188, +500.

step 1, order. With no masked layer (+487 clear everywhere, the common case) each layer's order o starts as its slot index and is then replaced, walking the list from the last layer down: q = the nearest layer below it in the list whose float rectangle overlaps its own (strict: q.x + q.w > x, x + w > q.x, the same for y, in float32); if there is one, o = (the slot index of q) + 1 (the lower layer's own index, not its renumbered one, because the walk goes top down); otherwise o stays its slot index. A layer therefore sits right after the nearest lower layer it overlaps, or keeps its own place.

step 2, key. key = mode | (4 x o + 4) with mode = 0 for kind != 0, else 1 when the drop-shadow byte +177 or the glow byte +178 is set, else 2. Keys are compared as unsigned dwords. The layers are sorted by key with MSVC's std::sort (StdSort_LayersByKey): up to 32 layers it is a stable insertion sort; with more it is the introsort whose partition (median of three up to 41 elements, Tukey ninther with step n >> 3 above, three-way partition) is not stable, so equal keys can swap (live: slots 58 and 51 with key 206 came out 58, 51). Then +12 is renumbered 1, 2, 3 ... by key change (equal keys share a number). The packing order is this sorted list.

step 3, the rare cases that change the order. A layer with +489 (mask source) is culled (+79 = 1, no packing, +16 = +20 = -1) when its rectangle does not overlap the nearest lower layer that has +487. A frame with +487 layers also runs a temporary allocation over the +487 layers (margin as below; at each temporary page break the later layers get +20 = the breaking layer's +12) and a third top-down pass that sets o = (o of the nearest overlapping lower layer) + 1 when that layer is a +487 layer with +179 set, kind != 2 and +78 / +486 / +488 clear, and o = 0 for a +487 layer that overlaps nothing; the overlap pass of step 1 then adds +20 to its result. None of this occurred in the live frame; it is read in the code only.

step 4, the integer rectangle. For each layer in list order, not culled: (x0, y0, x1, y1) = ((int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h)) (float32 sum, conversion truncates toward zero); w' = x1 - x0, h' = y1 - y0. margin m0 = 32 when |float +500| > 3.2 or float +180 > 3.2 or float +188 > 3.2, else 2.

step 5, the shelf (the primary shelf, page size W x H). State {cx, ry, rh, page} starts at {0, 0, 0, 0} each frame. For a layer that is packed (+179 set, kind <= 1, +78 / +486 / +488 clear) and has w' > 0 and h' > 0: mx = max(0, min(m0, trunc((W - w') / 2))), my = max(0, min(m0, trunc((H - h') / 2))); pw = w' + 2 mx, ph = h' + 2 my. (a) if cx + pw + 3 > W: ry += rh, rh = 0, cx = 0. (b) if ry + ph + 3 > H: page += 1, cx = 0, ry = 0, rh = 0. (c) x = cx + mx, y = ry + my. (d) if x0 is a multiple of 4 and x > 0 and x is not: padx = the distance up to the next multiple of 4, x += padx (else padx = 0); likewise pady for y with y0. (e) P = (x, y, x + w', y + h'); cx += padx + pw; rh = max(rh, ph + pady). The layer gets +16 = page, +208 / +212 = (float)x / (float)y, +216 / +220 = w' / h' as floats, +224 / +228 = x - x0 and y - y0 (the atlas offset: atlas pixel = screen pixel + offset), +240..+252 = the integer rectangle, +492 = 1. The content origin is P itself: the margin lies around it inside the pw x ph block that starts at (cx_before + padx, ry), so a layer with margin 32 at the start of a page has x = 32, y = 32.

step 6, special rectangles. A layer with w' <= 0 or h' <= 0 (the integer rectangle is empty) is returned unchanged: P = its integer rectangle, offset 0, the shelf does not move, +16 = the current page (live: layers of width 0 keep their screen y as atlas y). A layer that is not packed (+179 clear, kind > 1, or +78 / +486 / +488 set) allocates the whole page rectangle (0, 0, W, H): the margin is clamped to 0, both fit tests fail, so it takes a new page (page += 1, shelf left at cx = W, ry = 0, rh = H) and the next layer after it starts yet another page; its +16 = that page, its rectangle is not rewritten (+492 = 0).

step 7, masked layers (+487, read in the code only). The same rectangle goes first to the secondary shelf (own state {0, 0, 0, 0}, same margin, same alignment key, same rules) giving P2 and +20 = the secondary page; when the secondary page changed, the primary shelf is first moved to a new page (page += 1, cx = ry = rh = 0); then the primary placement runs as in step 5. +232 / +236 = P2 - (x0, y0), else = +224 / +228.

parity. The 2 x 2 box grid of RT 26 is anchored at the atlas origin, so the layer's pixel column i (from x0) sits at atlas column P.x + i and the cell grid pairs it with its right neighbour when P.x is even (same for rows with P.y). If x0 is a multiple of 4 and P.x > 0, P.x is a multiple of 4 (always even); if y0 is a multiple of 4 and P.y > 0, P.y is a multiple of 4. Otherwise P.x = (the sum over the earlier layers of the same row of w' + 2 m + padx) + m + 0, and since every margin is even, the parity of P.x is the parity of the sum of the earlier widths in the row plus their pads; P.y = (the sum of the earlier rows' heights, each the maximum of h' + 2 m + pady in the row) + m + pady. The first layer of a page starts at cx = 0, ry = 0.

worked check. Page 0 of the frame: slot 0, integer rectangle (44, 129, 150, 196), margin 32 (blur 6.0): x = 0 + 32 = 32 (44 is a multiple of 4: nothing to add), y = 32, P = (32, 32, 138, 99), cx = 106 + 64 = 170, offset (-12, -97); slot 1 has width 0 (rectangle (0, 253, 0, 308)): unchanged; slot 2 (595, 248, 692, 303), margin 32: x = 170 + 32 = 202 (595 is not a multiple of 4), y = 32 + 0 = 32, offset (-393, -216); slot 3 (603, 254, 684, 297): x = 170 + 97 + 64 + 32 = 363. All 63 layers match in x, y and page, 5 pages, margins of 2 and 32, rows opened by the x test and pages by the y test, and the alignment of 4-aligned origins.

notes: The checked frame was the idle Job Tree: slots 63 and above in the layer table held stale records (their +16 / +208 values are from older frames) and are not part of the list; the list array beyond the live entries also keeps stale entries (the count at +172 is cleared after the frame). A renderer that wants the atlas position of a layer needs only steps 4 to 6 once the packing order is known; the order depends on the overlap test, on the shadow / glow flags and on the sort's tie behaviour, so a frame with equal keys among more than 32 layers must follow the partition code (the sheets of the two std::sort loops and their partition helpers).
open_questions: ? the mask-layer flag +487 is written by ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent (V, 2026-10-30), and a live Job Tree frame had one (TextMask of the main tab: slot 4 with +16 = 5, +20 = 0, secondary shelf {178, 0, 124, 0}), which matches step 7 as written; the margin of that layer comes from stale radius floats of its reset record. ? the secondary shelf's meaning beyond its use for +487 layers (slot 30 / the mask atlas; GUILayer_CopyOffsetRegion reads +232 / +236). ? the heap-sort fallback of the sort is not modelled (it needs more than 20 partition levels). ? targets other than 1280 x 720 (the page size is read from the target object, so W and H follow it).

name: LayerBlitOverFrameTarget
summary: Store 2: the layer is blended onto the frame target by a pixel shader that reads the frame pixel through a UAV and writes it back: frame = layer + frame x (1 - layer alpha) in premultiplied form, per channel, from the layer's 8-bit pixel, stored again at 8 bits. The blend factors are in the shader arithmetic (ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA written out), not in the output-merger state.

behavior.text: pixel shader 0x006E60 (blend type 0, no offsets): S = layer pixel x cb9 + cb10 (default 1 and 0); out.rgb = frame.rgb x (1 - S.a) + S.rgb x cb8.z; out.a = frame.a x (1 - S.a) + S.a; skipped when S.rgb x cb8.z and S.a are all zero; cb8.z = 1.0 (live read of the UI manager float at +144; GUILayer_FillConstants writes it).

the layer pixel is read at uv + cb34.zw with the default sampler word (point) where uv = position / target size and cb34.zw = atlas offset / target size, the atlas offset being integral (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect), so the read is exactly texel (pixel + atlas offset).
the quad is the layer's integer screen rectangle (rect - atlas offset: x0 = (int)x, y0 = (int)y, x1 = (int)(x + w), y1 = (int)(y + h) of the unpacked rectangle); only those pixels are visited.
the store is a typed UNORM UAV store, so the float result is converted to 8 bits; on the test GPU an exact half stores the lower value (see UnormStoreRoundsHalfDown).

formula for a renderer, with Lp = the layer's stored 8-bit premultiplied pixel / 255 and Fp = the frame pixel / 255: F'.rgb = floor-half-down(255 x (Fp.rgb x (1 - Lp.a) + Lp.rgb)) / 255, F'.a likewise with alpha; layers are applied in the order of LayerCompositeOrder; the result is exact only when the layer pixels are the 8-bit values of store 1.
other blend types (digit 0 = 1..17) are other shaders of the same family; blend type 2 is a multiply (rgb = frame x (S + 1 - S.a)); the Job Tree uses type 2 for the Lv chips of the name tags.

notes: This record and LayerContentDrawnIntoCleared8BitTarget give the two stores; the second is exact only if the first is.
open_questions: ? the blend types other than 0 and 2 were not read formula by formula.

name: LayerCompositeOrder
scope: the order of layers and of draws on the frame
summary: Layers are composited in the order the game's draw traversal opened them, but only layers whose rectangles overlap are ordered against each other: each layer gets an order number that is one more than the creation index of the nearest overlapping lower layer, then the layers are sorted by (mode, order) and the order is renumbered densely. Within a layer the draws replay in the order they were recorded (children last-to-first, GUINode_DrawChildren).

behavior.text: the list of used layers is built from the layer pointer table in index (creation) order; the layer's own order starts as its index.

for every layer from the top of the list down, the nearest lower layer whose float rectangle (+208..+220) overlaps strictly (open intervals) sets order = that layer's current order + 1 (+ the page base); layers with no overlapping lower layer keep their index.

the sort key then used is mode | (4 x order + 4) with mode = 1 for an ordinary layer (kind 0) with the drop-shadow or glow group, 2 for another ordinary layer, 0 for a whole-layer-blur layer; the orders are renumbered densely by key change. The sort comparator itself (sub_1403C2B00) was not read.
the commands are executed by 64-bit key: target type, atlas page, pass (clear 1, draw 2, blit and effects 59), order; ties keep the recording order (stable merge sort in UIContext_SortCommands).
GUINode_DrawChildren draws a node's children from the last entry to the first, so the first UIB entry is on top; a Reference node draws its whole component where it stands in the list.

consequence for a renderer: composite the layers in creation order; layers that do not overlap can be done in any order; the pass order puts every layer's draws before any blit of the same atlas page and pages in ascending order.

open_questions: ? the exact comparator of the two sorts (equal keys) and whether a rectangle overlap test uses the effect margins (the rectangles are expanded by GUILayer_ExpandBounds before this runs).

name: LayerContentDrawnIntoCleared8BitTarget
summary: Store 1: a layer's UI draws go into the layer content target (RT 26, RGBA8 UNORM, 1280 x 720) inside the layer's atlas rectangle, which starts cleared to (0, 0, 0, 0), with the fixed-function blend ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA. The pixel shader's output is premultiplied, so the stored pixel is premultiplied colour and coverage alpha.

behavior.text: the draw target is the object in row 0 slot 0 of the per-type target table (Renderer + 0x5CA8 + 800 x type) and its resource is the one of slot 26 of the per-type slot table (RT 26) (live read: the two views hold the same resource pointer).

the blend word of an image draw is the draw state's first dword, set by UIRender_ApplyDrawState after the program apply; the default draw state (data at 0x1408FF878) holds 0x79420a11: blend on, SRC = ONE, DEST = INV_SRC_ALPHA, add, SRC_ALPHA = ONE, DEST_ALPHA = INV_SRC_ALPHA, add, write mask 0xF (fields decoded as BlendDesc_FromWords does: +1 on each 5-bit factor).

clear: GUILayer_Composite queues a type-0 command per cleared target once per atlas page (dedupe through dword_140906B5C, reset each frame by UIRender_PrepareLayers); the command carries the target view and 16 zero bytes of colour; its executor is a ClearRenderTargetView call (D3D12 command list slot +384 = index 48) with that colour.
the clear is per atlas page, not per layer: layers of a page occupy distinct rectangles (shelf allocator, margin 2 px) and the pass order puts the page's clear first.
the scissor rectangle of the layer's draws is (int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h) of the packed layer rectangle (atlas coordinates).

formula for a renderer: for each image pixel p covered by a draw, in draw order, L(p) = clamp(S(p) + L(p) x (1 - S.a(p))) per channel with S the premultiplied shader output, L stored as unsigned-normalised 8 bits after every draw; the first draw into an empty pixel stores round8(S). The rounding of a blend result at the ROP (ties) was not captured separately (the 8-bit shader stores round halves down on the test GPU, see UnormStoreRoundsHalfDown).

open_questions: ? rounding of fixed-function blend results at exact ties.

name: ListGadgetInputPath
scope: why a list cursor moves only when the screen calls the list input
summary: A list gadget's cursor moves by pad or keyboard only when the screen's input handler calls the list's own input; the Left / Right branches of the settings screen return before that call.

behavior.text: the settings input ends with `if (!UIListGadget_IsAnimating(list)) UIListGadget_OnInput(list, input)` when no value list is open and the row list takes input.
a screen of this class whose input handler lacked the call left the cursor on row 1 for Down and pad DOWN.

the shared menu input of the `UIFFTOMenuFunctionBase` part reads the same input bytes: +13640 / +13644 and +13642 / +13646 call part vtable +16 (delta -1 / +1), +13641 / +13645 and +13643 / +13647 call part vtable +24 (the title's TitleMenu_MoveCursor); then 0x1400F1278(input).
UIListGadget_IsAnimating is true while a 'Show', 'Slide_left' or 'Slide_right' state runs; GUINode_PlayState sets the state's running byte.

name: LookPoolOfFifteenIsWiredIntoFixedSlots
summary: The look pool's 15 records are not a constant that a same-length change can raise: the record block is followed at once by the scene-unit slots, each pool index owns fixed GPU upload positions or buffers, the HD sheet slots cover pools 0..9, and the battle snapshot holds exactly 15 records.

behavior.text: g_LookPool spans 0x140D005A0..0x140D3002A (15 x 0x32D6); the scene-unit in-use dwords start at 0x140D30030 and g_SceneUnitSlots at 0x140D30038.

14 functions address the block (LookPool_ClaimForSprite, LookPool_ResetForBattleLoad, CharaPalette_ReloadForShape, sub_14026E838, sub_14026C2E8, SceneUnit_RunPlacement, sub_14026929C, SceneUnit_SyncSpriteFromPool, sub_14026E0F4, sub_140273468, sub_1401D4544, sub_1401D46B0, sub_140210AF0, Battle_RestoreSceneVars); the count 15 is an immediate in LookPool_ClaimForSprite and an end address in the others.

sub_14026E838: pools 0..8 upload through sub_140260718 at positions derived from the index, pools 9..14 copy into 32 KB buffers 2..7 at 0x1437ADF4C + ((pool - 7) << 15) and 4 KB blocks at 0x1437B5F4C + 4096 * (pool & 7); a pool 15 would write from 0x1437EDF4C (other globals) and its pointer over dword_1411A37C8.
SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry: the HD sheet slot word is pool + 20 for pools 0..8 and 17 from 9; only pools 0..9 get an HD sheet entry (g_HdSheetEntryBySlot[20..28], dword_142E7FEE0).
Battle_RestoreSceneVars copies exactly 0x2FA8A bytes (15 records) from g_SnapshotLookPool, which lies in the 668,112-byte snapshot region a resume payload fills (sub_1402181EC).
a pool of more than 15 looks per load needs the records relocated, a GPU slot or buffer per new index, HD sheet slots for them, wider face values and a snapshot of its own.

name: LookSitesUseTheSaveRecordNotTheSlot
summary: The six portrait readers compute the look from the unit's marker, job byte and sex each time through six copies of one 211-word table; none of them reads the battle slot, and they are separate from the battle sprite path.

behavior.text: the sum 2 * job - 52 (+1 for women, jobs 92 and 93 adjusted) appears in those functions at 0x2C082F, 0x2B573F, 0x2DB44D, 0x3009BD, 0x300F95 and 0x32ABEA, each against its own copy of the table and a bound of 0xD3; none stores the number.
the six copies hold the same 211 words (compared word by word).

JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag computes a flag (job minus 74 above 19), not a sprite number; JobTree_FillJobRecords calls Unit_ResolvePreviewShape for generic jobs and stores the result through SpriteRecord_Fill (32-bit).

name: LookSlotsAlreadyInTheGame
summary: The battle loader already assigns small per-battle slots to looks: a 16-entry queue, 15 look pool records shared by equal sprite numbers, 16 scene-unit records and 10 HD sheet entries.

behavior.text: LookPool_ClaimForSprite returns the pool index of an equal sprite number or claims the first free record; an index of 15 or more is refused, so at most 15 distinct looks are loaded in one battle (the queue itself holds 16 entries, the unit table 21).
SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry stores the pool index at scene unit +9 and the sprite low byte at +0xA; SceneUnit_SyncSpriteFromPool copies pool +1 back into +0xA when the unit's pool record changes.

HD sheet entries are kept per pool index for 0 to 9 (dword table at 0x142E7FE6C + 4 * (20 + pool) and the dword at 0x142E7FEE0); SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry writes the entry from the HD table at creation and sub_140260CF0 fills it at the first draw when it is -1.
pool records 10 to 14 get the sheet slot 17, which only pool 9 fills; what they draw in HD is not seen.
the battle snapshot copies the queue, the whole pool and the HD slot dwords.

open_questions: ? what pool indexes 10 to 14 draw in HD (live check).

name: LookSumSeesTheBaseJob
summary: Five functions compute a save unit's portrait look index from its job byte (2 * job - 52, + 1 for marker 0x81), each against its own copy of the portrait code words. A job byte of 174..255 gives index 296..458.

behavior.text: in all five the code after the marker test is the same: marker 0x80 loads the job byte (record +2) and computes 2 * job - 52, 0x81 2 * job - 51, Mime (93) two less; the loaded byte is also copied for the job 91 / 92 tests (index 130 / 131); the index guard compares with 0xD3.
stock (211 rows) an index of 211 or more fails the guard and takes the no-code path.
the later job 160 / 161 / 164 tests read the job byte from the record again; a job in 74..93 never matches them.

name: MapDrawListRowsAreSearchedLinearlyToABoundOfFifty
summary: MapDrawLists_Load clears two 513-byte bitsets, then searches the 50 rows of the draw-list table for the row whose 16-bit map id equals the loaded map and sets, for each 0xFFFF-terminated list the row points at, the bit of every listed draw-record index. A map with no row leaves both bitsets empty.

behavior.text: rows are 24 bytes: map id (16 bits) at +0, six bytes of zero, a pointer to the first list at +8 and to the second at +16; the loop adds 24 bytes per step and stops after 50 rows.
the bound is a compare of the row counter with an 8-bit immediate (value 50); it is the only thing that ends the search when no row matches, and an immediate of this form holds at most 127.

a row whose id equals the map is followed through both pointers without a null test, so a matching row with a null list pointer reads address 0; a zero row (id 0) therefore answers for map 0 if the bound reaches it.

the first pointer's list fills the bitset at 0x142FF84A0 and the second's the bitset at 0x142FF8290; each bit index is the list entry taken as a 16-bit number, so entries run to 4,103 at most in 513 bytes.
the 78 stock maps without a row draw everything the classic renderer draws by default; the lists name the draw records that are treated specially.
the list with only the terminator exists in the data pool (it is the second list of map 127's row).

notes: Ids 2..127 appear in the 50 stock rows (map 127 last).

name: MapLoaderIndexesThreeTablesByASixteenBitMapId
summary: Map_LoadBattleData takes the battle map id as a 16-bit value and uses it, with no bound, as the row of three tables: the Move-Find rows (24 bytes), the map-block file numbers of the two text-language copies (4 bytes), and, through MapDrawLists_Load, a linear search over the draw-list rows.

behavior.text: the id is the argument as an unsigned 16-bit value; the Move-Find row is the 24 bytes at table + 24 x id, copied into a working copy of the battle; no comparison of the id with a row count precedes it.

the file number of the map block is the dword at index id of the table of the current text language (the table for language 0 when the language record says 0, else the other table); a value of 0 means the map has no block and the function returns without reading or loading anything else.
the map block is 4096 bytes read with GameData_ReadSectors(file number, 0, 0x1000, buffer): the locator holds a FILE number of the game's packed data, not a sector.

the draw lists are loaded only when the graphics-mode flag at 0x142E80048 is zero (the classic renderer's data); I: that flag is nonzero in the enhanced renderer, whose mesh load is gated on it being nonzero.
for each stock map 0..127 the function returns the buffer for the 123 maps that have a locator and null for the five that have none, and the Move-Find working copy equals the stock row.

notes: The two locator tables and the Move-Find table have exactly one instruction each that addresses them (census of the whole image).

name: MapMeshAndAnimFilesCarryTheirOwnMapId
summary: The mesh file and the anim file of a battle map hold the map id in their header, and the loaders refuse a file whose id is not the one requested. The renderer builds nothing for a refused mesh.

behavior.text: the mesh header is 48 bytes: a format tag, the map id at +8 and the layer count at +12; the loader compares the tag and the id and frees the buffer and returns 1 on a mismatch.
the anim header is 32 bytes with a format tag and the map id at +8; the loader checks them the same way.

the meshes of maps 1, 5 and 100 and the anims of maps 1, 2 and 100, unpacked from the game's own pack, each hold their own map id at +8; the mesh layer count is 1; the three anim files have the same size.
a mesh larger than 7,534,452 bytes is refused; ids 15 and 33 never load a mesh.

notes: A file placed under another map id's name therefore loads only if its header id is changed to match.

name: MapRendererTableRowFallbacks
summary: What each renderer table gives the build when a map has no row: nodes get default flags (visible), polygon overrides do nothing, system textures use the stock default file, map textures are an empty set, the anim file is requested, and a missing Map row skips the variation settings but not the mesh load.

behavior.text: node rows are looked up by (map, variation or 0), with a second try on variation 0; none found leaves every referenced node with its default flags and the visible bit set.
polygon rows are the whole set of the map; none means no override; a polygon row whose condition id has no row is skipped.
RefinedBgAnim without a row requests the anim file; a row of kind 0 does not.
the multi-keyed tables are searched through a sorted set index stored in the file, so rows for a new key need set records for that key to be found.

name: MapResourceFilesAreFileNumberAndSizePairsPerMap
summary: MapResource_Read reads one resource file of the current map: a request record either carries a file number and a size itself, or carries the marker value 0xFEEDBACC (as a 32-bit number) and a pair number, which selects a {file number, size} pair from the list the map's pointer in the per-map table names.

behavior.text: a request with its flag byte (+13) at 0 reads nothing; otherwise the file number is the dword at +2 and the size the dword at +6.

when the dword at +2 holds the marker, the table of the current language (language 0 or the other) is indexed by the current map id (32-bit global at 0x140784478) to a pointer; a null pointer ends the read with nothing read, a non-null pointer is a list of 8-byte pairs {file number, size}, read at pair number = the dword at +6.
a read happens only when the resulting size is not 0 and a destination is given; the read is GameData_ReadSectors(file number, 0, size, destination).
the two pointer tables have 128 entries each and exactly one reader; there is no bound on the map id there.
the lists live in shared read-only data, so a table row is a pointer into that pool, not a list of its own.

notes: A request that names its file number directly does not use the per-map list at all, so a map's resource files can be named inside the map block alone.

name: MapTextureRowsAreReadOnlyForMapIdsUpToOneTwentySeven
summary: The loader of the map's colour and lighting textures reads the RefinedBgTexture rows only when the map id is 127 or less; for a larger id it requests no map texture at all. The system textures have no such bound.

behavior.text: the id field of the texture set is compared unsigned with 0x7F before the table is touched; above it the slot count is 0.
the same loader also needs the texture-source field to be 0; that field's writer was not found (?).
MapTextures_LoadSystemSlots has no id compare: no row, or an empty name, requests the stock default colour table file.
other id compares on the path: MapMesh_StockNodeOffset returns at once above 116; MapMesh_Load skips 15 and 33.

census of the compares of the map id with 127, 128 or 255 over the renderer functions and every function that reads the three map-id globals: the texture loader's compare above is the only range test; the palette command in MapBlock_RunCommand tests map 127 for equality (a fixed branch, every other id takes the default); the other 7Fh and FFh immediates in those functions mask or test unit and node data, not the id.

the id is stored as a byte in the save header (the low byte of the battle map id), so 255 is the largest id the header can show; the id field of the texture set is a 32-bit copy of the loader's id, which is a 16-bit argument: ids 256 to 65535 are the only values above 255 that can reach the compare.

notes: Stock rows of the renderer tables end at id 116; ids 117..128 have no row and no mesh file.

name: MapTextureRowsPairEveryNameWithAFrameCount
summary: A RefinedBgTexture row has two name lists and, beside each, a list of frame counts stored as plain signed 32-bit integers. The name builder reads the count at the name's index and returns no name unless the frame number is below it, so a name with no count, or a count of 0, is never requested and its texture is missing.

behavior.text: the row has four array fields at +8, +16, +24 and +32: names (text offsets), counts (int32), names, counts; the first pair is read at the map variation index, the second at the kind-code index.

in all 1,338 stock rows the second count array has as many elements as the second name array (values 1, 5, 8, 10 or 30), and the first pair is equal in length except for one row with no names and one count.

with a frame series expanded by its counts (frame k replaces the final 0 of the name by k), every name of every stock row resolves to a file of its map's texture folder, file names compared without case; the exceptions are the names of map 0, which has no mesh.

the count 1 (bytes 01 00 00 00), read as an offset to text, points at the array's own second byte, a NUL: the cell is a valid reference to an empty string, so the bytes alone do not tell it from text (the type is known only from the reader's code).

notes: Seen live: with the counts missing the map's terrain textures were never requested (no texture file of the map was asked for); with the stock counts they were.

name: MenuListFlagFlow
scope: g_MenuList and the three list kinds that reuse it (shop, equip, ability), plus the job list
summary: The two high bits of the 16-bit list words are per-list-kind state, not part of the id: bit 14 is cannot-equip / cannot-learn / current, bit 15 is not written to g_MenuList at all but marks the equip-candidate buffers.

behavior.text: four builders set bit 14 on g_MenuList entries: Shop_BuildItemList (0x140288FBD, 0x140289061), Inventory_BuildEquipList (0x140288CAF), JobAbilityList_Build (0x1402869F3, 0x140286A2A) and sub_140286A78 (0x140286B81).
JobAbilityList_Build also sets bit 12 (0x140286A03) and bits 13+14 (0x140286A25); sub_14028A474 sets 0x1000 and 0x6000 on 8-byte ability rows.
no instruction writes bit 15 to g_MenuList: the only two 0x8000 list writers, sub_140287D9C (0x140288544) and sub_1402875A4, write their 5-word output buffers (g_EquipCandidates / stack).
seven functions read bit 14 of a g_MenuList entry: ShopEntry_Fill, sub_140332C54, sub_140332C8C, sub_140336664, sub_14036A994, sub_140366FE0 and sub_140333974.
no function in the exported set reads bit 15 of a g_MenuList entry; the bit-15 readers it does contain (ShopEntry_Fill 0x14036B4A9, sub_1402D5CC4) read the party equipment words instead.

the movers copy whole 16-bit words, so a flag travels with an entry through ItemOrder_FilterList (0x140285E7E, memmove 0x140285EA8), sub_140286228 (0x1402863AA), sub_140285B10 (0x140285BF6), sub_140285F2C (0x140285F57) and sub_140336B88 (0x140336D09).

two movers compare a whole word against a masked one and therefore never match a flagged entry: ItemOrder_FilterList compares order[i] unmasked to list[i] & 0x3FF (0x140285E63), and sub_140286228 inserts its row word unmasked but compares it to list[i] & 0x3FF (0x140286309).

sub_140285F2C can carry a flagged word into the saved order list off_14067F498[group], because it copies g_MenuList[0..] whole; its only caller builds the list in mode 0, so no flagged word was seen on that path.

notes: V: the sheets of the builders, row helpers and movers, and a 49-site table. The Outfitter carriers (g_EquipCandidates, g_EquipSet, the equipment words) are documented on their own records.
open_questions: ? whether any screen displays bit 12 or bit 13 of an ability entry; ? whether the demo/retail build differs in the ability-list modes.

name: MidBattleJoinLoadsLooks
summary: A unit that joins mid-battle is queued by Battle_AddJoinedUnit and loaded by running the look loader once per frame until it returns 0; the loader's file reads are synchronous.

behavior.text: the loader's step machine (g_LookLoaderState: pass, step, entry index; buffer 0x140CE3250) returns 0 once the entry index reaches g_LookQueueCount, 1 or 2 otherwise; its files are read with GameData_ReadSectors, which is synchronous (MemFile_Read clears the pending flag the high dword of qword_141856AB0 itself).

load step 2 stores a queue word above 170 back as 1 (stock clamp) and tests the word against byte +1 of all 15 look pool records, claimed or not (the loop over 0x140D005A1 in steps of 0x32D6); when one matches it reads no classic file, and the scene unit is built from whatever data the record its build uses holds.

name: MoveFindTakenBitsAreFourPerMapInA128ByteArray
summary: Which hidden tiles of a map have been taken is kept as four bits per map, two maps per byte, in a 128-byte array indexed by scene variable 51 (the current map id): map ids 0..255 fit, and the bytes after the array belong to the Poachers' Den stock. The same 128 bytes are saved, restored, snapshotted and cleared by whole-array copies.

behavior.text: the probe tests the bit 0x80 >> (tile slot + 4 x (id and 1)) of byte id / 2; the take sets the same bit. Neither compares the id with 256.

behavior.basis: (census of every instruction addressing the array, 2026-11-15)
behavior.text: nine functions touch it: the probe, the take, the save pack and unpack (whole-array 16-byte copies, 128 bytes), the battle snapshot capture and restore (both in one function, two copy runs), two further functions that copy the 128 bytes to and from another save structure, the party reset (clears the array byte by byte) and the function the database names Status_BuildFlagMasks, whose first statement clears the array with a 128-byte fill.
the array begins at 0x1411A7680 and the Poachers' Den stock array begins at 0x1411A7700, directly behind it: an id of 256 or more makes the probe read, and a take write, bytes of that stock.
the save pack puts the 128 bytes at a fixed offset (+34226) of the save work record, so a save carries bits for maps 0..255 only.
a hidden tile on a map whose row is all zero (no item, no trap) is still tile slot 0 at (0, 0) on layer 0; the probe finds it and reads the taken bit for any unit standing there.

notes: The earlier count of seven functions was by cross-reference from IDA, which misses accesses through the image base (the probe and the party reset).
open_questions: ? whether any save layout the game reads carries more than these 128 bytes for this purpose.

name: MoveRangeRules
scope: battle: the tiles lit when the Move command opens (and the same builder for the AI and for another unit's range)
summary: Which tiles a unit can stop on: a budget of Move + 1 spreads from its tile by steps and straight jumps under height, headroom, terrain-cost and occupancy rules; a final pass keeps the tiles it may stop on. Reproduced exactly by the debugger port on eight live captures.

behavior.text: budget: the start tile holds Move + 1 (Move capped at 124). Entering a tile leaves budget - cost(terrain of the entered tile) - the number of tiles jumped over. A tile is reached with a budget of 1 or more and can be left only with 2 or more. A better budget replaces a worse one; at equal budget the path with the smaller largest climb wins.

terrain cost (tile byte +0, low 6 bits), walking set: 1; 2 for terrains 14, 15, 16, 17 and 45; the weather cost (1..3, Battle_MoveRange_WeatherCost) for 9, 10, 11, 26 and 36; no entry for 18, 25, 28 and 63. The water sets cost 1 on the water terrains; the lava set also enters 18; the Fly / Teleport / float sets cost 1 everywhere except 63.

heights are half-steps: an edge of a tile is at 2 * height (byte +2) + slope (byte +3, low 5 bits) * k, k = two bits of the corner byte +4 for that edge (shift 0 = the +x edge, 2 = -x, 4 = -y, 6 = +y).

a step compares the edge left with the edge entered plus 2 * the entered tile's water depth; the difference, up or down, must not exceed 2 * Jump (Jump capped at 7; 31 for Fly or unit +0x9C bit 0x02).

headroom: the unit's body (6 half-steps; 4 Toad / Chicken; 8 with the float flag) must fit under the lowest underside above it at both ends of the step; an underside is 2 * (height - thickness) + the slope term of the other layer's tile, thickness = tile byte +5 low 5 bits.
slopes: a tile whose slope exceeds the unit's Jump, or is 3 or more on a one-axis slope (corner byte & 5 equal to 1 or 4), can be entered or left only downhill.

horizontal jump: in a straight line over 1 .. Jump / 2 tiles (Jump 3 -> 1 tile), never onto a higher level, each tile passed costs 1 extra; a column in the gap blocks when its tile or an enemy on it overlaps the unit's body at the height it leaves from, or lies entirely above that height. Fly and Teleport do not jump.

other units: an enemy's tile is not standable, so it cannot be entered or crossed (it blocks a jump too); an ally's tile can be crossed but not stopped on; KO and Jumping units are not obstacles but nobody stops on their tile; Crystal and Chest units are ignored (their tile can be stopped on).

mounts: a tile holding an ally of job 94..96 without a status of group 10 and with no rider is lit for a unit that can ride (unit +0x06 bit 0x80 or 0x40, not Toad / Chicken, unit +0x65 bit 0x20 clear).

water: depth 1..3 tiles are standable for a walker; depth 4+ only with flags 0x80 / 0x40; stopping needs depth <= 2 (3 with any of flags 0xD0); unit +0x9D bit 0x10 keeps the unit out of water altogether.
stop conditions besides the budget: slope <= 3 (<= 2 on a one-axis slope), tile byte +6 bits 0x80 and 0x02 clear, terrain not 28, terrain 18 only with flags 0x20 / 0x08, never the start tile.

Teleport (unit +0x9D bit 0x04 or 0x08, not as Toad / Chicken): every tile gets budget 1, so every tile that passes the stop conditions is lit. Fly (unit +0x9E bit 0x04, not as Toad / Chicken): open cost set, Jump 31, no climb bookkeeping; enemy tiles get the 'step onto' flag.

the result is written to tile byte +5 bit 0x20 only when the battle manager's marking state (dword +6536) is 15; other callers write the same set to a state bit of the marking table and leave the tile bits as they were.

Orbonne (Ramza, Move 5 Jump 3, three turns) and Gariland (five units, Move 3..5 Jump 3). Removing any one of these rules breaks at least one capture: the horizontal jump and its length, the gap test, water cost 2, the extra cost per jumped tile, no upward jump, the height limit (exact to the half-step, both directions), slope-aware edge heights, enemies block, allies cannot be stopped on, KO tiles cannot be stopped on, tile byte +6 bits 0x03 not standable.

not exercised by any capture (code only): headroom under a second layer, steep-slope refusal, forbidden terrains, depth 3+ water, the weather cost, Fly / Teleport / float and the water and lava abilities, Toad / Chicken, mounts and riders, the 16-entry blocker limit.

notes: The debugger port (its moverange module) runs the same passes in the same order as the routine, with an offline self-test over the captures. Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? Captures that would settle the code-only rules: a two-layer map (a bridge) with a unit under and on the bridge; a unit next to deep water (depth 3 and 4); a steep roof or stair of slope 3+; a unit with Fly, Teleport, Float or a water ability; a mounted chocobo; rain or a storm on a swamp map (weather cost); a battle with more than 16 other units.

name: MusicCommandWordHasEighteenOperandsAndSixOfThemOnlyWriteZeroOrTestNonzero
summary: The 16-bit word at 0x14186246A (the music id and slot of the command state) is addressed by eighteen instructions in seven functions; six of them only clear it or test it for nonzero, twelve read the id or the slot or store a new value.

behavior.text: census of every rip-relative operand into the word: sub_1402F109C at 0x1402F1145 (dword zero), 0x1402F1243 (low byte compared with dil), 0x1402F1265 (word read for the replay id), 0x1402F1283 and 0x1402F12BC (word zero), 0x1402F1298 (word read as the queue parameter); EventCmd_ServiceRequests at 0x1402F17DB (word read, low byte compared with the request) and 0x1402F17F0 (slot byte); sub_1402F2500 at 0x1402F250A (low byte test), 0x1402F2513 (slot byte) and 0x1402F254D (store); EventCmd_SetParamBlock at 0x1402F26E5 (low byte store); EventCmd_ActivateSlotParam at 0x1402F26F6 (word test) and 0x1402F2700 (slot byte); EventCmd_ReleaseSlot at 0x1402F2A98 (word test), 0x1402F2AAD and 0x1402F2AB9 (slot byte) and 0x1402F2AC8 (word zero).

the four slot-byte reads in EventCmd_ServiceRequests, EventCmd_ActivateSlotParam and EventCmd_ReleaseSlot (two) and the one in sub_1402F2500 load the high byte with a sign extension; the word itself is read with a sign extension in three places.
the register that sub_1402F109C compares with the low byte at 0x1402F1243 (dil) is zero there (cleared once at 0x1402F10C6 and not assigned again before the compare).

notes: Nothing outside these functions addresses the word; the command state is copied whole (16-byte moves) into the five saved context slots, which is how the word reaches a save.

name: MusicIdTravelsAsAByteInTheScriptPathAndAsADwordInTheTransitionPath
summary: The music sound id (1-based; the file is `sound/music/music_%05u.sab` of id minus one) reaches the music player by four routes with different widths: a command byte, a 16-bit state word shared with the slot number, a 32-bit event variable and queue parameter, and a 32-bit field of a data table; the 101-row music slot table is read in two functions and its values are never used.

behavior.text: the table at 0x14067FBB0 is read at six operands in two functions (MusicSlot_FetchRecord and a copy of its body inside a scene task); the index is 3 x a 64-bit sign extension of the id; the three dwords go to the request state and from there to a block at 0x140D3A8E4; nothing reads them (census of 39 operands of 0x140D3A8E0 to 0x140D3A91F).
the track file is named from the id by a format string; the cache key is the id as a 32-bit hash; the stock packs hold music_00000 to music_00099 (ids 1 to 100); no id above 100 has a file.

route 1, the class 32 command, passes byte 9 of its record; route 2, event variable 94 (a 32-bit cell), is passed whole but only while the word at +0x2C of the command context (0x14186246C) equals 1; route 3, the audio queue parameter, decodes the id as its low byte and the slot as bits 8 to 11; route 4, the BGMTransition and SoundEnhanced tables (nxd 306 and 280), passes the 32-bit field at row +16 of the SoundEnhanced row to slot 1.

the 16-bit state word at 0x14186246A (a field at +0x2A of the 56-byte command context that the save keeps five times, not a standalone global) holds id | slot << 8; the only writers of its high byte store 2 (or zero), so the slot byte is 2 whenever the word is nonzero.
the story event opcode 0x84 does not use this path: it plays file number operand plus 44 directly (operand a byte, I).

notes: An id of 256 or more written by route 1 or 2 would overwrite the slot byte; route 4 already carries ids above 255 into the table read.
open_questions: ? whether the sound engine opens a music file that is not in the stock pack index; ? which retail scripts write event variables 92 to 94 (none found by byte pattern).

name: MusicParameterOfTheAudioQueueIsASmallConstantOrTheCommandWord
summary: Every stock producer of a kind 1 (play music) entry of the audio command queue passes either a small constant or the 16-bit command word of the command state; no stock parameter has a bit above 0x2FF set, so bits 12 and up of the parameter are free.

behavior.text: the push function sub_14033FDAC takes (kind, parameter); a kind 1 entry is pushed by exactly two bodies: sub_14034004C (its own argument, after an optional kind 2 entry and before a kind 3 entry) and, as plain constants, two direct pushes (parameter 0x11B in sub_14033F8C0, 0x221 in the function at 0x140370E14).

the direct calls of sub_14034004C load ecx with 0x11B (four calls), 0x220 (two calls in the function at 0x1403793DC, one of which is also reached with 0x21A), 0x221 (two), 0x223 (one), or the sign-extended 16-bit command word (sub_1402F109C at 0x1402F1298); no call passes a computed value.
the worker sub_14033FE00 decodes a kind 1 parameter at 0x14033FFC3..0x14033FFCF: the slot is bits 8..11, the music id is the low byte (movzx of dil), and everything above bit 11 is ignored.
the command word of a stock game only holds values below 0x300 (the id is a byte and the slot byte is 0 or 2), so a stock parameter is below 0x300 on every route.

notes: Indirect calls (through a function pointer) were not searched: none of the direct pushers is a table entry, and the queue is private to the audio command functions.
open_questions: ? a push through a function pointer (none found).

name: MusicTrackFilesAreOpenedByNameThroughTheFileManager
summary: A music change queued on the audio command queue ends in EventMusic_LoadTrack, which builds the file name sound/music/music_NNNNN.sab from the track number (the music id minus 1) and opens it through the game's file manager by that path.

behavior.text: queuing kind 1 with the parameter of id 5 in slot 2 made the queue service load track 4 on channel 8.
loading a track not already held passes the path sound/music/music_NNNNN.sab to the file manager's path resolver.

notes: Seen 2026-11-16 on the Steam PC build.

name: NamedCharactersKeepTheirOwnLookWhateverTheirJob
summary: A named character (character byte +0 of the save, party or battle record below 0x80, e.g. Ramza 0x01) keeps its own sprite and portrait whatever job it holds; Ramza's change with the chapter. A generic unit (0x80 male, 0x81 female) is drawn with its job's look, the male or female version by that byte.

behavior.text: named characters do not change model or portrait with the job; Ramza's changes with the chapter.
in battle, with Knight (76) in his job byte, Ramza's figure on the battle Status screen was his blue Chapter 1 sprite; the generic units of the party drew their jobs' sprites on the Change Job grid.
the shape resolvers read the character byte before the job (a byte below 0x80 selects the character's own shape row).

name: NewUnitsGetStartingJpInEveryJob
scope: engine (starting JP of a new unit)
summary: A new unit (a spawn: battle entries, the New Game party, recruits built by Unit_BuildFromRecord) gets starting JP in every job by the game's own rule for stock jobs (Unit_InitJobJp: the curve's value at the level plus up to 99).

behavior.text: Unit_InitAbilitiesFromJob runs Unit_InitJobJp for indices 0..19 only; Job_LevelFromTotalJp gives level 0 below RequiredJobExp[1] (100 in the stock curve), so a job with no starting JP is at level 0.
a job at level 0 shows 'Lv. --' and no JP on the unit panels.
every stock job a unit may have held 100 or more total JP (only the gender-locked index 17 / 18 rows were 0).

open_questions: ? a recruit at the Warriors' Guild not checked live.

name: NxdTableRebinding
scope: loaded nxd tables and the localized reload
summary: An nxd table can take a new file while the game runs: its load callback NxdTable_BindRows may run again on a bound table, and the game's own language switch reloads every localized handle through it.

behavior.text: NxdTable_CreateHandle builds a 168-byte NexResourceHandle: flags +92 |= 0x2008 (bit 3 = 8 is the flag the language reload selects); +96 / +112 the invoker (Callback_InvokeWithHandle) and NxdTable_BindRows with the table object as context; +128 / +144 the invoker and NxdTable_OnReady (sets the table's state +12 to 2 when the handle's load status +80 is 1, else 3).
NxdHandle_OnLoaded (NexResourceHandle vtable 0x140721600 slot 8) calls the invoker at +96 with (context, &callback at +112, &handle), so the load callback runs as NxdTable_BindRows(table, handle).

NxdTable_BindRows frees and reallocates the entry array only when the new row count is larger, otherwise rewrites the entries in place; a table without the contiguous-keys flag has its lookup arrays freed and built again on use.

an item name table bound again at the title screen showed the new name in the Outfitter Buy list and the main menu Inventory list on the next screen (item names are read from the bound table when a list is drawn, not cached at start), also after four rebinds in one session; no crash.

the weapon power the Outfitter's detail panel shows is read from the weapon record (through the weapon record lookup, 0x1402B8C74) when the panel is drawn: a changed record at the title screen showed on the next visit.
ResourceManager_ReloadLocalized walks the resource hash for handles with flag 8, so a language change reloads the nxd tables through this path; the code says yes, it was not traced live.

name: OrderInsideItemGroup
scope: the order of item ids inside one menu group (the item menu, the equip screen and the shop list)
summary: Three rules decide the order, in this priority: the saved order list is the order, membership maintenance inserts a newly owned id at the front and removes a lost one, and an explicit sort replaces the order with a field-by-field comparison. The field schedules live in data; the key getter, the comparator and the two sorters are the only code that imposes an order.

behavior.text: the saved list is the order. A consumer either copies the list or filters the menu list through it, so the output keeps the list's order and every id the list does not hold is dropped.
membership maintenance inserts a newly owned id at index 0, removes an id that is no longer owned and leaves every other entry where it is; it never sorts.

an explicit sort replaces the order. Modes 0..7 select byte lists of item record fields from the table at 0x14067FAB0, and the insertion sort swaps when the comparator's key difference is zero or more.

the keys are the equipment category byte with 19 remapped to 100 (field 0), the price (1), a sub-record byte (2), two equipment bytes (3 and 4), the total owned plus equipped count (5), the name string (9), the id (10), a flag true for one chosen id (11) and the item text row's dword at +0x28, or 999999 when the row is missing (12); fields 6, 7 and 8 have no key.
the obtain-order case is a filter, not a sort: field 8 first keeps only the ids the obtain-order list holds, then moves one chosen id to the front.
the menu candidate builder caps its output at 145 ids and stops its id walk at 0x104; the order filter uses a 264-word stack buffer.
swapping on an equal key makes the sort unstable: two ids with the same key exchange places instead of keeping their saved order.
because the two screens keep independent lists (A for the item menu, B for the equip screen) the same item can sit at different positions in the two menus; no function reads both lists together.

notes: V: the three rules, the field table and the key table; the screens' names are labels taken from the builders and the UI state they read.
open_questions: ? the screen names: no string or scene id in the image names the item menu or the equip screen, so the labels are inferred from the builders and the UI state they read.

name: OutfitterPreviewReadsRecordPastItemBlockWithSessionFlag
summary: The Outfitter preview builder, the equip-clear price step and the equip commit each reduce a party hand word to an item id with an AND that must strip the session flag (bit 15); an AND whose mask keeps bit 15 turns the id into 0x8000 + id, and Item_GetRecord, which does no range check, then reads a 12-byte record 32,768 rows past the item block.

behavior.text: in the stock code bit 15 of a party hand word means 'picked or bought in this Outfitter session' (sub_1402D7280 stores id | 0x8000 and adds the price to the running total); the preview builder takes the id as word AND 0x3FF (mask loaded at 0x1402D7027), the equip-clear step as word AND 0x3FF (0x1402D64AA), the commit as word AND 0x3FF (0x1402D6609); the mask strips the flag and every id bit above bit 9.

the preview builder (sub_1402D6FB8) extracts bit 15 by a shift (0x1402D704C), prices a flagged slot with the record's +8 price, and posts the five id and price pairs through sub_140295558; the equip-clear step (sub_1402D6464) subtracts the price of a flagged slot from the running total and stores an unflagged word in the override array; the commit (sub_1402D65D4) strips the flags of every party word, returns each stored original to the inventory and clears the override array.

Item_GetRecord has no bound check: an id below 0x100 indexes one 12-byte table, any other id indexes the second table by 12 times the id, so an id of 0x8000 + n reads the record 393,216 bytes after the record for n.

with the flag left in the id, the Fitting preview of a picked item showed a blank After row and the stat compare of the wrong record; for two ids (16,383 and 20,000) it raised one access violation inside sub_1400FA7AC and the game stopped answering; a stock item previewed without a fault.

the fault needs the unrelated record to carry an attribute byte of 0x55 or more: sub_1400FA7AC then sets its attribute-record pointer to null and loads through it. Whether a given pick faults depends on what memory follows the item block, not on the item.

the same wrong id in the equip-clear step subtracts the price of the record past the block from the total, and in the commit makes the new word differ from the stored one at the 'not changed' compare, so a pending slot always takes the new-item-flag branch; the code path was read, not seen.

with the strip mask 0x7FFF (the exact id mask), a flagged word and a plain word give the same id for every id from 0 to 32,767, and the preview, buy-and-equip, cancel and the Status equip behaved with the item's own name, icon, stats and price at ids 300, 16,383, 20,000 and 32,000.

notes: The census of the other equip-session masks (0x1402D59CB, 0x1402D5F3D, 0x1402D60F3, 0x1402D6A50, 0x1402D6B1E, 0x1402D72F3, 0x1402D7314, 0x1402D7392, 0x14028B67F): I, each reads a word without the flag or an id that is never flagged. The equip-change function sub_1402D7280 refuses a word with bit 14 set (test at 0x1402D72A0) and its callers pass a plain id; the cancel (sub_1402D5B6C) and commit decide 'session word or plain id' by comparing the word with 0x4000, which a plain id of 16,384 or more also passes.
open_questions: ? what the Optimal Fitting button does with a picked id of 16,384 or more (not run).

name: PartyJobWordIsSixteenBits
scope: engine (party and save records, Jobs screen)
summary: The party record's 16-bit job word (+0x24) carries a job id above 255 through the Jobs screen, the status header and the skillset lookup; only the save record's byte (+2) cannot.

behavior.text: rebuilding the party record from the save record (leaving and re-entering Status) puts the save byte back into the word.
a job list entry above 1023 needs the mask at the start of JobTree_FillJobRecords (3FF) widened.
nothing else was seen reading the party word as a table index; the readers that only compare the id (the 9 sites of the research census) were not each exercised.

name: PartyWriteBackCopiesSecondarySetAndReactionLowByteInOneLoop
summary: PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave copies two bytes in one two-pass loop: the low byte of the party record's secondary command word into save +7, then the low byte of the equipped reaction word into save +8; the reaction's high byte goes to save +9 on its own. The party record is then rebuilt from the save record.

behavior.text: the loop walks the party words at +0x60 and +0x62 (2 bytes apart) and stores each word's low byte into save +7 and +8; +0x63 is copied to save +9, and the support and movement words' bytes to save +10..13.

behavior.basis: (seen live 2026-11-17, a watch on both records)
behavior.text: equipping a reaction stored the word in party +0x62, the write-back copied it to save +8 / +9, a fill cleared the party record and PartyUnit_FillFromWork wrote save +8 / +9 back into party +0x62.
so whatever the write-back stores at save +8 is what the unit has equipped after the rebuild: an equip that the write-back alters is undone at once.

notes: The equip path: sub_140333338 -> sub_14028916C (stores party +0x5E + 2 * slot, then rebuilds through sub_140285A6C).

name: PassiveAbilitiesAreAPerUnitBitMap
summary: A battle unit's reactions, supports and movement abilities are kept as an 88-bit map (ids 422..509) in bytes +0x94..+0x9E of its record, rebuilt from the innate ability words and the three equipped words; the game's tests of a passive are bit tests on that map.

behavior.text: Unit_SetAbilityBit(unit, id) ignores an id outside 422..509; otherwise it sets bit 0x80 >> (index & 7) of byte +0x94 + (index >> 3) with index = id - 422, and an id below 454 also becomes the unit's equipped reaction word (+0x14).

Unit_BuildAbilityBits clears the 11 bytes, then sets the bit of each of the four innate words (+0x0A..+0x10) and of the equipped reaction (+0x14), support (+0x16) and movement (+0x18): seven calls, in that order.

callers of the rebuild are the unit build and reload paths (UnitWork_BuildFromSave, Unit_BuildFromRecord, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow, Unit_ReloadFromJobRowEx, sub_140275EF4); sub_14030B4F0 calls Unit_SetAbilityBit directly.

the last three bytes of the map (+0x9C, +0x9D, +0x9E: the movement ids 486..509) are the bytes the move range builder reads as movement flags (see the UnitWorkRecord members move_flags_c, move_flags_d, move_flags).

byte +0x99 bit 0x80 is the map's bit for id 462 and is the bit that halves an action's MP cost (sub_1402828E4, sub_14030B1A0); +0x99 bit 0x40 (id 463) is the JP Boost test of the JP award (BattleActionJpFormulaAndSpillover).
that 462 is the Halve MP support and 463 JP Boost: by their effects only; the names were not read from the text table.
the after-damage chain tests +0x94 bits 0x80, 0x40, 0x20, 0x02 and +0x95 bits 0x40, 0x20, 0x10, 0x08 and +0x96 bits 0x40, 0x10; see AfterDamageReactionChain.
whether other code tests bits of the map that was not found (the study read only the places named here); the compares of ids 422..509 over the whole executable were not counted.

notes: Offsets are those of the 512-byte battle unit record (table at 0x141853CE0).
open_questions: ? whether unused passive rows (443, 481, 484, 485) have a reader anywhere (not searched exhaustively).

name: PassiveListsJoinTheCurrentAndStockJobs
summary: The reaction, support and movement lists of the Status screen join the rows of the unit's current job and of the stock jobs 75..92 only.

behavior.text: sub_14028A8B0 calls JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows for Party_GetUnitJobId's job and then for job ids 75..92; in modes 2 / 4 / 6 a job JobList_BuildForPartyUnit does not hold is skipped.

open_questions: ? a list longer than the game's 200 rows.

name: PerJobSlotStateLayouts
scope: engine (party, battle and save unit records)
summary: Per-job state (learned flags, level nibbles, JP, total JP) sits in several unit layouts at different offsets, indexed by the job slot that Job_IdToIndex returns.

behavior.basis: (the offsets and counts are not re-read by us)
behavior.text: the save record (0x258 bytes) keeps learned flags at +0x32 (3 bytes a slot), level nibbles at +0x74, JP words at +0x80 and total JP words at +0xAE, with 23 slots (0 to 22) in each array; the party-menu copy (0x280 bytes) keeps learned flags at +0x7B + 3 * slot, level nibbles at +0xBD, JP words at +0xCA and total JP words at +0xF8; a battle unit (0x200 bytes at 0x141853CE0) keeps learned flags at +0xA2 = (slot + 0x36) * 3, level nibbles at +0xE4, JP words at +0xF0 and total JP words at +0x11E.

the job level thresholds come from the 'generaljob' NXD table (rows 0 to 19, nine thresholds each: 0, 100, 200, 400, 700, 1100, 1600, 2200, 3000); slots 20 and above have no row, so JobLevelJp read garbage for them.
slots 20 and 21 are the hidden Dark Knight and Onion Knight (jobs 160 and 161) and are not always empty in a stock save.

behavior.basis: (live 2026-11-13, a party unit on slot 49, world map)
behavior.text: the save-record offsets +0x74 / +0x80 / +0xAE and the party-menu copy's +0xBD / +0xCA / +0xF8 hold (current JP words identical in both); the party copies sit behind the pointer table at 0x141800F50 (the unit's save slot at copy +44; two copies for one unit). Writing only the level nibbles (8) in both does not last: on the unit's next menu screen the party copy's nibbles were back to the levels its total JP gives. With the total JP words at 3000 (the Lv. 8 threshold) in the save record and both copies, the Change Job grid and the Job Tree showed Lv. 8 after the unit's Status was opened again (not while the screens stayed open).

name: PlaceNameOfABattleComesFromTheMapRowOfTheLoadedId
scope: engine (battle title card, pause menu, save list)
summary: The title card, the objective header of the pause menu and the place label of the save list all show the place name belonging to the loaded map id's Map row, and a mid-battle autosave resumes the battle on the saved id.

behavior.basis: (seen live, id 120 with a Map row equal to map 84's)
behavior.text: the title card read 'Balias Tor' (map 84's name); the pause menu's objective header read 'Balias Tor' above 'Defeat all enemies!'; the save list labelled the Pre-battle and Mid-battle autosaves 'Balias Tor'.

after loading the Mid-battle autosave the battle resumed on the same terrain with the saved unit whose turn it was (slot 17 of the party), the word at 0x140D4012C read 0x78 (120), and the pause menu was usable.
a pause-menu 'Return to World Map' after the resume went to the world map normally; a victory returns to the world map after the victory page and the closing balloons.

name: PlaceTextOfAMapIdComesFromTheMapRowAndTheTownRow
scope: engine (battle HUD, save list, title card)
summary: The battle's place text reads the place-name id at row +8 of the Map row of variable 51; the save list reads row +12 (else +8) of the Map row of the low byte of the map id for a battle save, and the Town row of the location otherwise; the title card is a picture chosen by variable 51 minus 1.

behavior.text: SaveHeader_FillBattleFields stores variable 49 at header +0x29 and the low byte of the 32-bit battle map id at +0x2C; the resume capture keeps the id as 32 bits.

the save list's place label uses the Map row (table 60) of an 8-bit value for a slot with the battle flag and the Town row (table 52) otherwise; a map id of 256 or more therefore shows the place of its low byte, and a missing Map row gives an empty label.
the battle HUD place text is the PlaceName title of the id at Map row +8, with the map taken from variable 51 when the battle state machine enters state 0x4B.
EventMapTitle_LoadTexture takes variable 51 minus 1 as the index and keeps it when it is 119 or less (signed compare), else 0; the classic path loads maptitle_%03d.tex with it.
with the enhanced flag and graphics level 2.0 or more the scene entry stores the unclamped map id minus 1, and the HD sheet binder uses that index plus 193 as the entry of its fourth slot.

notes: The Map data table has ids 0..128 in the shipped data; map ids 127 and 128 have no place id.
